items.title: New Delhi police detain top 'cockroach' leaders after flash protest at Jantar Mantar
items.description: India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said on Tuesday that key leaders had been detained after entering an iconic protest site in New Delhi blocked by police. Opposition parties and supporters of the movement have taken to the streets in recent days, defying a security clampdown to demand the resignation of the head of India’s election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party. The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing. Delhi Police said on Monday that Jantar Mantar in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites. The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence . But a video posted online by CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday showed protesters clambering over the barricades, running into the empty space and waving the national flag — before police chased and detained them. View this post on Instagram “CJP sneaks inside to reclaim Jantar Mantar,” the group said in a post on social media, adding that those detained included leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde. “All of them have been detained by Delhi Police,” it added. View this post on Instagram Delhi Police had announced three official sites on Monday as alternatives to Jantar Mantar, where protesters have gathered for decades — including CJP demonstrations that led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal in July. “You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke said, tagging Modi in his post. View this post on Instagram Modi, in comments at a business conference in New Delhi on Tuesday, called India the “mother of democracy”, but did not refer directly to the protests. “In our country, people openly debate a wide range of issues and discuss different perspectives,” he said.

items.title: Who’s Emelia Affi Agbenyo, the 43-year-old newly sworn-in Deputy EC Chair?
items.description: The swearing-in of 43-year-old Emelia Affi Agbenyo as one of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission has stoked controversy following her affiliation with the incumbent National Democratic Congress (NDC). The young international development cooperation professional is on record as having served as a spokesperson for the NDC on governance in the 2024 general elections. Since her appointment, social media has been awash with some posts she made in the past that were deemed political in support of the NDC. A video of her speaking on a media platform as a representative of the NDC has also gone viral. As a result, many have questioned her independence and neutrality in such a sensitive office. For many of the critics, they’re particularly unhappy that the NDC, which criticised previous EC officials and tagged them as politically aligned to the New Patriotic Party (NPP) have gone ahead to do the same. But who is Emelia Affi Agbenyo and what else is she known for? Before her appointment to the EC role, she was Deputy Director General in charge of operations at the Ghana TVET Service. As an international development cooperation professional, Emelia Affi Agbenyo has worked in strategic leadership, corporate governance, public sector management, and international development administration. Career path Her experience spans diverse sectors, including inclusive governance, skills development, private sector and enterprise development, donor negotiations, institutional capacity strengthening, public sector reform, and stakeholder engagement. As Deputy Director General in charge of Operations at the Ghana TVET Service, she provided executive oversight of nationwide operations, driving organisational performance, institutional transformation, and policy implementation. She is passionate about inclusive governance, gender equality, and social inclusion, and has led numerous initiatives advancing gender transformation, particularly within the informal sector. Her work reflects a strong commitment to strengthening governance systems that promote equity, participation, and opportunities for marginalised groups. Emelia Affi Agbenyo Her leadership experience spans policy design, organisational development, resource mobilisation, and managing complex multi-stakeholder partnerships. She has successfully led large-scale national and donor-funded programmes in inclusive policy implementation, skills and enterprise development, and gender transformation. She has managed strategic partnerships with organisations including UNDP, USAID, KOICA, GIZ Ghana, and the former Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training. Beyond her executive role, she serves as a Commissioner of the National Development Planning Commission of Ghana and a Board Member of the African Trade Chamber and Education and Aspirations. Education Emelia Affi Agbenyo holds a Master of Arts (Hons) in Education Management & Leadership from the University of Ghana, Legon; a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and Linguistics also from the University of Ghana; and is currently pursuing a Master’s in International Relations at GIMPA. She also holds a Master’s in Education, Leadership and Management from GIMPA. She pursued General Arts at Chemu Secondary School in Tema, where she completed her studies in 2002.

items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale ce mardi 13 octobre 2026: Al Ahdath almaghribia Les travaux de la gare Casa-Sud se poursuivent selon le calendrier prévu, pour un investissement de 1,3 milliard de dirhams. Le projet ambitionne de faire de cette infrastructure un pôle de mobilité urbaine, accueillant différents types de trains et assurant une connexion directe avec le réseau routier, le tramway, les autobus et les taxis. L’objectif est de faciliter les déplacements et d’améliorer la correspondance entre les différents modes de transport collectif à Casablanca. Bayane Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI a adressé un message de félicitations au Président de la République de Guinée équatoriale, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, à l’occasion de la fête nationale de son pays. Dans ce message, le Souverain a également réaffirmé Sa forte détermination à continuer d'œuvrer de concert avec le Chef de l'État équato-guinéen pour consolider les liens fraternel unissant les deux pays et renforcer la coopération bilatérale fructueuse et constructive, afin de la hisser au niveau des aspirations des deux peuples frères et de contribuer à la réalisation de la sécurité, de la stabilité et de la prospérité du continent africain. Annahar almaghribia La Confédération Générale des Entreprises du Maroc (CGEM) se mobilisera pleinement pour traduire en actions concrètes les Hautes Orientations contenues dans le discours prononcé par SM le Roi Mohammed VI devant les membres des deux Chambres du Parlement, a affirmé son président, Mehdi Tazi. « Nous travaillons à la formalisation d’un plan d’action du secteur privé, articulé autour de priorités claires, à savoir accélérer l’investissement productif dans l’ensemble des régions, renforcer l’innovation et l’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle dans nos entreprises et développer de nouvelles filières industrielles et de nouveaux secteurs d’exportation », a-t-il souligné. Assahra almaghribia Son Altesse Royale le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan a présidé, lundi au Parc d’expositions Mohammed VI d'El Jadida, la cérémonie d'ouverture de la 17e édition du Salon du Cheval d'El Jadida, organisée sous le Haut Patronage de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, sous le thème « Le cheval au service de l'humain ». L'ouverture par SAR le Prince Héritier de ce Salon, qui se poursuit jusqu’au 18 octobre, traduit la haute sollicitude dont Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI n’a eu de cesse d'entourer le secteur équestre et la ferme volonté du Souverain de structurer durablement cette filière, de l'élevage jusqu’aux compétitions internationales, et d'en promouvoir le rayonnement à l'international. Al Haraka La Banque centrale des Émirats arabes unis (CBUAE) et Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM) ont coprésidé la 7e édition du Forum des instances charaïques centrales, organisée aux Émirats arabes unis, avec la participation de représentants de plusieurs pays, notamment le Koweït, la Malaisie, la Turquie, le Nigeria et l’Ouzbékistan. Dans un communiqué relayé par l'Agence de presse des Émirats (WAM), la Banque centrale émiratie a souligné que la tenue de ce Forum intervient dans le cadre du partenariat stratégique et de l'étroite coopération unissant les deux institutions, ainsi que des efforts conjoints visant à renforcer la coordination et l'échange d'expertises dans le domaine de la finance islamique. Al Massae La Chambre des représentants tient ce mardi une séance plénière consacrée à l’élection de son nouveau président, selon un communiqué du président du bureau provisoire de l’institution. Cette séance s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en place des structures de la Chambre, à la suite de l’ouverture de la douzième législature. Bayane Al Yaoum Le renforcement de la coopération entre le Maroc et les États-Unis dans les domaines de la recherche et de l’innovation agricoles a été au centre d’échanges, à Rabat, entre la directrice de l’Institut national de la recherche agronomique (INRA), Lamiae Ghaouti, et une délégation de l'Association nationale des départements d’État de l’agriculture (NASDA). Ces discussions ont eu lieu lors d'une visite de ladite délégation au siège de l'INRA, s'inscrivant dans une dynamique de rapprochement entre les deux institutions marquée par plusieurs missions et échanges depuis 2024 et visant à identifier les complémentarités scientifiques et techniques et à explorer de nouvelles perspectives de partenariat. Pope Leo heads to Rome hospital for lung operation
items.description: Pope Leo XIV was due to be admitted to hospital in Rome on Tuesday for surgery to remove a nodule on his lung, an operation experts say is generally low-risk. The 71-year-old will head to the Gemelli hospital in the late morning, Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni told AFP . The surgery to remove a pulmonary nodule, or small growth of tissue in the lung, will mark the pope’s first hospitalisation since he became head of the Catholic Church on May 8, 2025. On Sunday, in a surprise announcement following Angelus prayers, Leo told faithful in St Peter’s Square that doctors had discovered the nodule “at a very early stage” during recent medical checks. “The doctors believe it would be right to intervene,” he said, addressing the crowds from a window of the Apostolic Palace. The Vatican was historically very secretive about papal health, but began to be more transparent during the illness of Leo’s predecessor Francis , an Argentine who freely discussed ailments. The pope’s recovery time could be about a week, the Vatican said. His audiences have been cancelled until October 20. Rome’s Gemelli hospital is where popes are usually treated, and Leo is expected to stay in a special top-floor suite, under high security. He will likely be accompanied by his personal nurse Massimiliano Strappetti, who looked after Leo’s predecessor Francis during several stays at the Gemelli hospital before his death last year . ‘Coin lesion’ Chicago-born Leo, the first US pope, is sporty and believed to generally be in good health. Marco Scarci, a thoracic surgery expert in the UK, told AFP it was not “a particularly risky operation” and he expected Leo’s recovery to be quick, though “it might take up to three months to return to his pre-surgery fitness level”. Leo is scheduled to travel to South America from November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Most pulmonary nodules are benign, or non-cancerous, but a small percentage can be an early indication of lung cancer. The Vatican told AFP the nodule was found during routine health checks, and there were no symptoms that led to checking the pope’s lungs. A small nodule is called a “coin lesion” because on X-rays it looks like a coin, Professor Federico Venuta, head of Thoracic Surgery at the Policlinico Umberto 1 hospital in Rome, told AFP . Small nodules tend not to cause symptoms, but larger ones can cause shortness of breath, chest pain and persistent coughing — sometimes with blood. Such nodules “could be a whole range of benign lesions — inflammatory, infectious, autoimmune, or congenital — or they could be malignant,” Venuta said. Outlook ‘positive’ Removing the nodule can take place under general anaesthetic with the patient breathing through a tube. “Often, the lesion can be accessed from the outside or inside, for instance, via image-guided biopsy or endoscopy, but sometimes this is not possible,” Venuta said. Even if the nodule should turn out not to be benign, the pope’s outlook would be “very positive”, he said. “For a generally healthy person, the prognosis for lung cancer caught at such an early stage — specifically a pulmonary nodule with no distant spread — is absolutely favourable,” he said. In terms of the Latin American trip, Venuta said that “generally, the rule is to avoid air travel for about 20 days following these surgeries, though there is obviously some flexibility”.

items.title: Kerrygold Strengthens Ties with Nigeria’s Baking Community at Cake Expo 2026
items.description: Kerrygold reaffirmed its commitment to Nigeria’s growing baking community through its partnership with the International Cake Exploration Societe, Nigeria (ICES, Nigeria), at Cake Expo 2026, held on October 7 and 8 at All Seasons Plaza, Ikeja. The two-day expo brought together bakers, cake artists and enthusiasts from across the industry for an engaging experience focused on creativity, learning, networking and the business of baking. As the lead sponsor, Kerrygold leveraged the platform to connect directly with members of the baking community, creating opportunities for interaction, product discovery and sampling. At the Kerrygold booth, attendees sampled the brand’s products and explored their applications in baking. Beyond product discovery, the booth provided a platform for bakers and enthusiasts to engage with the brand, share experiences and learn more about the products that support their craft. For Kerrygold, the partnership reflects the brand’s commitment to building stronger relationships with bakers and supporting the wider ecosystem that continues to drive creativity and growth within Nigeria’s baking industry. “At Kerrygold, we recognise the passion, creativity and expertise that bakers bring to their craft. Our partnership with ICES, Nigeria gives us an opportunity to connect with this community, understand their needs and support the platforms that help them grow and thrive.” — Titilayo Ijiyokunola, General Manager, Ornua Dairy Products Nigeria Ltd. The collaboration with ICES, Nigeria further strengthened Kerrygold’s engagement with the baking community, providing a platform for the brand to connect with bakers where they come together to learn, network and showcase their creativity. Through its participation in Cake Expo 2026, Kerrygold continues to foster meaningful relationships with bakers and demonstrate its commitment to supporting the people and businesses shaping the future of baking in Nigeria. About Kerrygold Kerrygold is a globally trusted Irish dairy brand renowned for its quality, rich taste and provenance. Built on generations of dairy knowledge and heritage, Kerrygold is made with the finest milk from grass-fed cows and quality ingredients, with no artificial ingredients. In Nigeria, Kerrygold Milk is manufactured and distributed by Ornua Nigeria, bringing the brand’s distinctive rich, creamy taste and heritage to consumers across the country. items.title: Cyberattaque inédite en France : des frigos portés à 50°C dans des centaines de supermarchés
items.description: Cette attaque massive a frappe Intermarche, Cooperative U, Carrefour, Monoprix et E.Leclerc. Les meubles froids de rayons entiers se sont transformes en etuves, condamnant des stocks a la destruction. Je confirme qu’une cyberattaque touche depuis cette nuit les installations de production de froid de plusieurs magasins de notre réseau @CooperativeU. Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées, en lien avec les frigoristes, pour rétablir la situation au plus vite. Une enquête devra permettre de faire toute la lumière sur cette attaque. S’attaquer à des équipements essentiels à la conservation des produits frais et à l’approvisionnement alimentaire des Français est d’une extrême gravité et est inédit. C’est inacceptable. — Dominique Schelcher (@schelcher) October 12, 2026 Le president-directeur general (PDG) de Cooperative U Dominique Schelcher a denonce sur le reseau social X une action « d'une extreme gravite et inedite » visant « des equipements essentiels a la conservation des produits frais et a l'approvisionnement alimentaire des Francais ». Une faille dans des logiciels obsoletes Les pirates ont exploite d'anciennes versions du logiciel de regulation Danfoss (systemes AK-SM800 et AK-SC355), encore largement deployes et connectes a Internet sans reseau prive virtuel (VPN). Ces equipements en fin de vie ne recoivent plus de mises a jour de securite. En forcant un degivrage continu, les auteurs de l'attaque ont fait grimper la temperature des installations a 50 °C. a Haguenau (Bas-Rhin), la gerante de l'Intermarche Sophie Matt a constate les degâts : « Les pirates sont parvenus a propulser de l'air a 50 °C dans nos congelateurs. » Elle evalue ses pertes a 50 000 euros. Le bilan grimpe jusqu'a 200 000 euros dans certains hypermarches. Au moins 300 points de vente Intermarche et Netto, pres d'une centaine de Cooperative U, 80 Carrefour et 5 % des Monoprix ont ete touches. Le hacker SaxX, tres present sur les reseaux sociaux, estime de son cote qu'« il est difficile de faire une attribution dans les premieres heures de l'attaque informatique ». J'ai pu débattre sur le plateau de @DariusRochebin , ce soir sur @LCI, pour parler de la cyberattaque hors-nome sur les centaines de frigos de la grande distribution... à cause des failles de danfoss ! Hélas, le retour à la normal sera plus long que prévu ! On se rend compte que faire de la cybersécurité est bien plus compliqué que prévu. Se pose la question de qui est derrière une telle cyberattaque, ce à quoi je répondais qu'il est difficile de faire une attribution dans les premières heures de l'attaque informatique. Néanmoins, on est clairement pas sur un groupe cybercriminel avide d'argent ce qui laisse d'autres pistes encore à explorer comme une puissance étrangère ou un groupe d'hacktovistes ou des petits cyber malandrins... tous très bien préparés à l'évidence pour lancer une telle cyberattaque coordonnée avec une bonne connaissance terrain néanmoins... [...] — SaxX ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ (@_SaxX_) October 12, 2026 Le parquet de Paris a ouvert une enquete, confiee a l'Office anticybercriminalite, apres des « departs de feu » signales. L'Agence nationale de la securite des systemes d'information (Anssi), saisie par le Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu, a identifie la vulnerabilite et appele a deconnecter ces controleurs d'Internet ou a renforcer le filtrage reseau. a l'echelle nationale, les pertes se comptent deja en millions d'euros, avec un gaspillage alimentaire massif. Cette nouvelle attaque illustre un peu plus la vulnerabilite numerique de la France, comme le souligne l'editorialiste Francois Lenglet. 📢 « Nos frigos, nouvelle cible des hackers », le parti pris de notre éditorialiste économique François Lenglet @FLenglet « C'est une attaque qui expose une nouvelle fois la vulnérabilité de nos systèmes, surtout les plus banals » #24hPujadas #LCI #hackers #frigos #France⤵️ https://t.co/y6GJCVCH9G — 24h Pujadas (@24hPujadas) October 12, 2026 Un rapport choc de l'Anssi, paru durant l'ete, pointait deja du doigt les failles de l'etat francais en matiere de cybersecurite avec notamment une centaine de failles en deux mois seulement.

items.title: Algérie : une enseignante alerte sur les ravages des smartphones sur les élèves
items.description: Une enseignante lance un véritable cri d’alarme sur les ravages des smartphones sur les élèves algériens. En se rendant à l’école où elle enseigne, cette enseignante adresse un message aux parents à la suite d’un constat alarmant : ses élèves sont complètement groggy en classe. Impossible pour eux de se concentrer sur les cours tellement ils arrivent dans un état d’épuisement le matin. La raison va vous surprendre : non, ils ne veillent pas pour réviser leurs leçons mais pour scroller sur leur téléphone portable jusqu’à pas d’heure ! Attention, les smartphones font des ravages à l’école Inquiète quant à l’avenir de ces écoliers, l’enseignante qui a réalisé cette vidéo s’adresse d’abord aux parents : « On souffre avec nos élèves en classe car ils sont complètement déconnectés en cours. Il faut absolument leur retirer leur téléphone portable à la maison » exhorte-t-elle dans une vidéo partagée sur les réseaux sociaux. Puis elle explique que ses élèves font carrément des nuits blanches, scotchés à leurs écrans. « Lorsque je demande à l’un d’entre eux : qu’as-tu mon fils ? tu as l’air éreinté, il me répond ‘j’ai veillé jusqu’à 2 heures du matin connecté à mon téléphone’. Dans la foulée, un autre élève me confie avoir dormi à 4 h du matin », révèle-t-elle visiblement interloquée. Et d’ajouter : « C’est la première fois que je vois des enfants déconnectés à ce point de leurs études ! » « Vous hypothéquez votre avenir ! » Dans la seconde partie de la vidéo, l’enseignante adresse un message aux élèves et leur recommande de ne pas hypothéquer leur futur en sciant la branche sur laquelle ils sont assis : « Pensez à votre avenir, vous êtes nos enfants, on vous aime, on ne vous veut que du bien, et vous vous tuez de vos propres mains en vous connectant 24 heures sur 24. La connexion va vous bousiller et vous tirer vers l’arrière » s’écrie-t-elle. Cette enseignante de la commune d’Aït Smail (Bejaïa) a jeté un pavé dans la mare. À travers cette vidéo elle tente de sensibiliser parents et élèves aux dangers d’une utilisation excessive des écrans. Passer la nuit à regarder des films et des vidéos sur le téléphone portable au lieu de respecter les heures de sommeil provoque des difficultés de concentration et une baisse des résultats scolaires. C’est aux parents de faire preuve de fermeté et de vigilance en limitant l’utilisation des smartphones par leurs enfants et en les leur retirant la nuit, afin de leur garantir un sommeil réparateur, de préserver leur santé et d'accroître leurs chances de réussite dans leur parcours scolaire. À bon entendeur… L’article Algérie : une enseignante alerte sur les ravages des smartphones sur les élèves est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Maracana de Garghin : Les «Talents cachés de Cissin» remportent la 9e édition
items.description: • La finale du Maracana s’est jouée, dans la soirée du 11 octobre 2026 • L’équipe de Cissin a battu celle de Garghin aux tirs aux buts • Le promoteur, Dr Yves Kafando, Directeur général des Douanes, satisfait de la compétition La finale a enregistré la présence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement La finale du Maracana du quartier dd Garghin, compétition initiée par le Directeur général des Douanes, Dr Yaves Kafando, a drainé du monde dans la soirée du dimanche 11 octobre 2026 sur le terrain de Garghin. Parmi les spectateurs qui ont fait le déplacement se trouvaient le Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin Simporé, les Ministres Secrétaire général du Gouvernement, Ousmane Ouattara, Directeur du cabinet du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Anderson Medah, de la Justice et des droits humains, Edasso Bayala, de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le Commandant Pélagie Kaboré, de la Sécurité, le Commissaire divisionnaire de police Mahamadou Sana, de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Serge G. Poda,le Ministre délégué chargé des ressources animales Amadou Dicko et bien d’autres invités de marque. Un promoteur satisfait du déroulement de la compétition Dr Yves Kafando, promoteur du Maracana de Garghin La compétition, débutée le 4 juillet 2026, a enregistré la participation de 24 équipes de la ville de Ouagadougou. Pendant plus d’un mois, elles se sont livrées à des joutes sportives ayant permis de désigner les deux équipes finalistes. Pour le promoteur, cela est un motif de satisfaction. «Nous sommes entièrement satisfaits de cette édition. L’esprit de fair-play a prévalu tout au long de la compétition. Nous tenons également à témoigner notre reconnaissance à toutes les personnalités qui ont effectué le déplacement pour nous accompagner et contribuer à la réussite de ce tournoi. En tant que promoteur, je peux affirmer que je suis pleinement satisfait. Depuis la première édition jusqu’à aujourd’hui, le tournoi a considérablement grandi et gagné en maturité, notamment sur le plan organisationnel», s’est satisfait Dr Yves Kafando, DG des Douanes et promoteur du tournoi. Les anciennes gloires ont livré un match en lever de rideaux contre des jeunes de Garghin La présence d'invites de marque était exceptionnelle au regard de leur nombre. Pour le patron des Douanes burkinabè, cela est la preuve de leur soutien au sport. «Le sport est un facteur de paix, de cohésion sociale et de rapprochement entre les populations. Or, notre pays a besoin de cohésion, d’entente, d’amour et de fraternité. Il était donc tout à fait naturel que les autorités soient présentes pour nous accompagner dans cette initiative. Cette mobilisation témoigne de leur esprit de fraternité et de leur volonté de soutenir les initiatives sportives», a-t-il indiqué avant d’ajouter que c’est aussi la preuve que le tournoi bénéficie d’une attention particulière au sommet de l’Etat. Une finale bien disputée avec la victoire de l’équipe de Cissin Les populations de Garghin et les passionnés du football ont répondu présents lors de la finale La finale a opposé l’équipe de Garghin à celle de Cissin. Dès le coup d’envoi, elles ne se sont pas donné un round d’observation. Les jeunes de Garghin, encouragés par le public, lancent les assauts contre le camp adverse mais leurs tentatives restent vaines. D’abord dominés dans le jeu, les joueurs de Cissin finissent par se retrouver et apportent la réplique. Tout comme l’adversaire, les attaques restent stériles. La pause intervient sur un score nul et vierge. A la reprise, le jeu devient encore plus intense surtout avec les promesses dont une motocyclette au premier buteur de la soirée. Les occasions se succèdent mais ne sont pas concrétisées. La partie se termine sur ce score de zéro partout. Selon le règlementaire de la compétition, l’arbitre fait recours aux tirs aux buts pour désigner le vainqueur. A l’issue des 3 essais, l’équipe de Cissin parvient à inscrire un but contre zéro pour les jeunes de Garghin. Des prix aux équipes L’équipe «Les talents cachés de Cissin» sacrée championne du tournoi L’équipe «Les Talents cachés de Cissin», victorieuse, est repartie avec des médailles d’or, le trophée, 4 ballons, un jeu de maillots et la somme de 750.000 francs CFA. Les finalistes malheureux ont reçu des médailles d’argent, un jeu de maillots, 4 ballons et une enveloppe de 500.000 francs CFA. La formation de Kamsog-Tenga FC, classée 3 e , est repartie avec un jeu de maillots, des ballons et la somme de 250.000 FCFA. Espoir FC, équipe Fair-play a également reçu un jeu de maillots, des ballons et la somme de 250.000 FCFA. Le meilleur espoir, le meilleur gardien du tournoi avec 2 buts encaissés et le meilleur buteur avec 4 réalisations ont tous été récompensés. Faire du tournoi un cadre de détection de jeunes talents Le maracana est à sa 9 e édition. Un chemin parcouru et qui inspire de grandes ambitions au promoteur. Ainsi Dr Yves Kafando souhaite faire du tournoi un cadre de détection de jeunes talents. «Notre ambition est de faire de cette compétition un véritable cadre de détection et de promotion des jeunes talents. Nous voulons permettre à de jeunes joueurs prometteurs de se révéler et, pourquoi pas, de défendre un jour les couleurs nationales», a-t-il indiqué. Pour cela, des promoteurs de centres de formation et des responsables de clubs seront associés à l’initiative afin de permettre l’éclosion des jeunes talents. L’activité a aussi été marquée par un don de vivres aux personnes vulnérables. En effet, un opérateur économique a décidé d’offrir séance tenante 200 sacs de riz aux personnes vulnérables de Garghin. Ce don sera remis au chef du quartier qui en assurera la distribution. Jacques Théodore Balima (Collaborateur) L'historique du tournoi La 8 e édition, jouée en 2025, avait été remportée par Kamsog-Tenga FC. Cette équipe avait battu l’Union des Jeunes Solidaires aux tirs aux buts après un match nul de zéro but partout (0-0, t.a.b 2-1). La finale avait aussi mobilisé de nombreux acteurs du football burkinabè et de passionnés du ballon rond. Au fil des ans, le Maracana de Garghin s’est imposé comme un rendez-vous important des acteurs du football. The post Maracana de Garghin : Les «Talents cachés de Cissin» remportent la 9e édition appeared first on L'economiste du faso .

items.title: 5 of a family found dead inside locked flat in Karachi's Bin Qasim
items.description: Five members of a family were found dead on Tuesday in a locked one-room apartment in Karachi’s Bin Qasim Town, police said. Those dead included a middle-aged couple, along with their two daughters under the age of six, and the husband’s sister who was in her early 20s, according to Bin Qasim Station House Officer (SHO) Faisal Rafiq. Police said the apartment in Gulshan-i-Falaknaz Block J was locked from the inside. The SHO said the couple had suffered fatal injuries, adding that a pistol was recovered from the incident site. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar and the provincial police chief ordered that the deaths be probed from all possible angles. The Edhi rescue service said the bodies had been transferred to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC). Home minister takes notice Taking notice of the incident, the home minister sought details from the Malir senior superintendent of police (SSP). In a statement, Lanjar directed that the incident be investigated from all angles and that “every possible measure” be taken to bring the facts and motives to light. “The elements involved in the incident should be identified and action should be ensured according to the law,” Lanjar was quoted as saying. He ordered officials to keep him updated on progress in the case. Meanwhile, Sindh Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho sought a detailed report from the east deputy inspector general, a statement issued by his office said. “A transparent and impartial investigation covering all aspects of the incident must be conducted, and the actual causes of the deaths determined,” IGP Odho said. He also directed officers to ensure immediate evidence collection and fulfilment of legal requirements, including forensic analysis. He added that potential criminal angles should be probed and directed officers to keep him updated on the investigation. Last month, a middle-aged doctor, his wife and their three underage daughters were found dead at their Ahsanabad apartment in Scheme-33 off Superhighway. IGP Odho had established a high-powered body to investigate the incident.

items.title: AMATO demands justice for assaulted truckers by foreigners in Nigeria
items.description: By Godwin Oritse The Association of Maritime Truck Owners (AMATO) has condemned the alleged assault, molestation and dehumanising treatment of a Nigerian truck driver, Mr. Rilwan Olajide, and his motor boy, Mr. Taiwo Yinusa, at the premises of Karma Agric Feed & Foods Ltd, located at Km 12, Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, opposite the old Ratcoc Quarry, over the weekend. According to information, photographs and video evidence made available to the association, showed that the two transport workers were allegedly physically assaulted and intimidated by Indian nationals, with the alleged involvement of company staff and security personnel, following a disagreement over their demand for demurrage compensation. AMATO described the incident as a serious violation of human dignity that requires urgent police investigation, stressing that no commercial dispute could justify violence, intimidation or degrading treatment of workers. The association maintained that disagreements over demurrage payments must be resolved through lawful and peaceful means rather than force or abuse. It urged relevant authorities to investigate the incident, establish the facts and ensure that anyone found culpable is brought to justice. Citing Section 34(1)(a) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, AMATO noted that every person is entitled to respect for the dignity of their person, while torture and inhuman or degrading treatment are prohibited. The association stressed that the constitutional guarantee applies to everyone within Nigeria, irrespective of nationality, occupation or social status, adding that Nigerian transport workers deserve protection from assault, intimidation and other forms of abuse in the course of their legitimate duties. In a statement by Mr. Sani Mohammed, National Secretary General Association of Maritime Truck Owners, the group considers it unacceptable for any individual or corporate establishment to act as though Nigerian laws do not apply to them. Foreign nationals and corporate organisations operating in Nigeria are equally bound to respect the country’s laws and the fundamental rights of its citizens. Part of the statrment reads:”The Association unequivocally condemns all forms of racial discrimination, xenophobic hostility, intimidation and unlawful violence against Nigerian maritime truck operators. We will not tolerate any attempt to intimidate or dehumanise our members and other transport workers in the course of their legitimate duties. “Consequently, AMATO calls on the Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Alagbon, and the relevant investigative authorities to conduct a thorough and impartial investigation, identify all persons involved, preserve available evidence and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable in accordance with the law. “We further urge the management of Karma Agric Feed & Foods Ltd to cooperate fully with the investigation and take appropriate steps to prevent any recurrence of such an incident. “AMATO emphasises that this position is directed at the reported conduct of the individuals involved and not at Indian nationals or any other nationality as a whole. Our demand is for justice, accountability, equal protection under the law and respect for the dignity of every Nigerian worker. “The Association remains committed to protecting the welfare, safety and legitimate interests of maritime truck owners, drivers and motor boys who contribute significantly to Nigeria’s economy and supply chains.” The post AMATO demands justice for assaulted truckers by foreigners in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: L'Arabie saoudite dispose de l'un des dispositifs de defense aerienne les plus coûteux du Moyen-Orient, avec des batteries Patriot, des systemes THAAD ( Terminal High Altitude Area Defense ), des radars a longue portee et l'appui americain. Mais les dernieres attaques contre Riyad ont montre qu'aucun bouclier n'est etanche. Le probleme tient d'abord a la saturation. Les Houthis combinent desormais drones, missiles de croisiere et missiles balistiques dans une meme salve, afin de forcer les radars et intercepteurs saoudiens a traiter simultanement plusieurs menaces. Une enquete a ete ouverte apres les frappes meurtrieres contre l'aeroport King Khalid. Les defis de Riyad Deuxieme difficulte : les trajectoires. Les missiles balistiques sont relativement faciles a reperer lorsqu'ils montent haut dans l'atmosphere. Les drones et missiles de croisiere, eux, peuvent voler tres bas, suivre le relief et apparaître plus tardivement sur les ecrans radar. Cette complementarite sert a ouvrir des breches dans la defense saoudienne. Troisieme faiblesse : l'immensite du territoire. L'Arabie saoudite couvre plus de deux millions de kilometres carres et doit proteger en meme temps sa capitale, ses aeroports, ses raffineries, ses ports, les installations d'Aramco et ses bases militaires. Il est impossible de concentrer partout le meme niveau de protection. Les Houthis exploitent cette dispersion et changent regulierement de cibles. Enfin, le royaume fait face a une contrainte de munitions. Les stocks d'intercepteurs Patriot et THAAD ont ete fortement sollicites depuis le debut de la guerre contre l'Iran et restent coûteux a reconstituer. Tirer des intercepteurs a plusieurs millions de dollars piece pour detruire un drone beaucoup moins cher pose aussi un probleme economique et logistique. Cela ne signifie pas que la defense saoudienne soit inefficace : une large majorite des projectiles sont interceptes. Mais il suffit qu'un seul missile passe pour provoquer des dizaines de victimes et une onde de choc politique majeure. C'est precisement sur cette asymetrie que misent les Houthis.

items.title: Haruna Iddrisu calls for limits on annual university accommodation fee increases
items.description: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has proposed a framework to regulate annual increases in accommodation charges at public universities, suggesting that adjustments could be guided by inflation and set within a range of five to 10 per cent. He called for a committee to examine accommodation costs and recommend permissible annual increases to Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson under the Fees and Charges Act. Speaking in a media interview, Mr Iddrisu expressed concern about high rents and said a defined adjustment mechanism could help make university accommodation costs more predictable. “We do not support exorbitant rent prices being charged across the country,” he said. “It is my view that we should constitute a committee to advise the Minister of Finance before he proceeds with the Fees and Charges Act on what percentage increase is permissible each year.” The Minister suggested that prevailing economic conditions should inform any recommended adjustment. “We can say, for instance, take inflation as a guide, 5 to 10 per cent increase annually,” he added. The proposed committee would assess an appropriate benchmark for increases, with the aim of limiting arbitrary or disproportionate adjustments to accommodation charges. The five to 10 per cent range remains a suggestion by the minister, rather than an approved cap.

items.title: Wike, Soludo, Adeleke make APC’s revised 2027 campaign council list
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has named Nyesom Wike, minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT); Ademola Adeleke, Osun governor; and Chukwuma Soludo, Anambra governor, as state campaign coordinators in its expanded presidential campaign council for the 2027 general election, despite their affiliations with other political parties. Wike belongs to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Soludo is a member of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), while Adeleke won re-election as Osun governor in 2026 under the Accord Party. Under the new arrangement, Wike will coordinate the APC campaign in Rivers State and the FCT, Soludo will oversee Anambra, while Adeleke will coordinate the campaign in Osun. The expanded list is scheduled for inauguration by President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja on Wednesday. The APC initially released its campaign council list on August 22, naming Abdulaziz Yari, former Zamfara governor, as director-general. Senate President Godswill Akpabio, House of Representatives Speaker Tajudeen Abbas and Yobe Governor Mai Mala Buni were appointed deputy director-generals. In the revised list, Akpabio, Abbas and Kwara Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq are deputy vice-chairmen I, II and III, respectively, while Buni becomes deputy director-general I for the North. The council also includes former governors and party chieftains as advisers, which include former APC national chairmen Adebisi Akande and Abdullahi Adamu; former Ogun State Governor Ibikunle Amosun; former Osun State Governor Iyiola Omisore; Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo; Senator George Akume; former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba; and Wale Edun. Obafemi George is listed as an adviser on media. The Directorate of Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation, established ahead of the 2027 general election, has Faleke as Deputy Director-General, with Stella Okotete and Engr. Abdullahi Garba Ramat serving as Secretary I and Secretary II, respectively. Audu Maikori is also listed as a secretary. Other members of the directorate include Soares Omotola, Bashir Dabo, Sheriff Mohammed Usman, Jibrin Bancir, Ayoola Peter Olajolo, Abubakar Sadiq Sada and Princess Folasade Ogunbiyi. The post Wike, Soludo, Adeleke make APC’s revised 2027 campaign council list appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Man City, PSG clash at contrasting time for state-backed projects
items.description: Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain have reshaped football with the financial backing of Gulf state owners, but there is a stark contrast in the health of those projects ahead of their latest Champions League meeting on Wednesday. City return to Champions League action for the first time since they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules in a bombshell verdict which could threaten their place in the English top-flight. PSG strived to follow City’s era of sustained success and are now firmly established as Europe’s top dogs after successive Champions League titles to go along with their domination of French football. Abu Dhabi-backed City won the race against Qatar-owned PSG to become European champions first in 2023. The triumph over Inter Milan in Istanbul that completed a treble of Champions League, Premier League and FA Cup was the pinnacle of City’s rise since a 2008 takeover fronted by Sheikh Mansour, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates. But a cloud now hangs over City’s haul of silverware from the past 15 years unless they can overturn the findings of an independent commission on appeal. City were found to have used “sham” commercial deals with Emirati companies to inflate revenue and reduce costs to the tune of over £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018. No sanction has yet been meted out, but a severe points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League are among the potential punishments. – Al-Khelaifi shows support – The Premier League season has been thrust into turmoil while clubs await the appeal verdict, with City sitting top of the table after six successive wins, including a 3-0 rout of Liverpool on Sunday. Winning the Champions League could be City’s only way back into the competition next season. To do so they will need to stop PSG’s quest to join a very select club of sides to win the Champions League or European Cup in three consecutive seasons. Further UEFA action against City is unlikely as the club successfully fended off European football’s governing body when they attempted to act on the same leak of documents in 2018 that led to the Premier League’s case. In 2020, City were found guilty of breaking UEFA’s Financial Fair Play rules, fined 30 million euros ($34 million) and banned from playing in European competitions for two years. But City successfully overturned the ban at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which ruled that most of the alleged breaches “were either not established or time barred”. In the early days of FFP rules, both City and PSG entered into settlement agreements with UEFA in 2014. But the French champions have managed to steer clear of such issues since, with president Nasser Al-Khelaifi becoming an influential figure, both as a member of the UEFA Executive Committee and chairman of the European Football Clubs (EFC) organisation. At a meeting of the EFC in Copenhagen last month, Al-Khelaifi showed support for embattled City CEO Ferran Soriano. “His career is fantastic and Manchester City did a lot of positive things also, but I am not in a position to judge,” said Al-Khelaifi. “I think that they have the right to appeal, so it is not the final decision.” But a crisis which could eliminate City as a Champions League rival for years to come would be another win for PSG on the field, giving Qatar the upper hand in the soft power battle with regional rivals the UAE. items.title: 'No choice': IMF says developing countries must cut spending despite Iran war shock
items.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned on Tuesday that while low-income developing countries were dealing with the disproportionate impacts of the Iran war-fuelled energy shock , many had “no choice” but to cut spending or potentially face debt restructuring. Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the organisation’s Annual Meetings in Bangkok, IMF deputy director of research, Petya Koeva Brooks, said that the heavily indebted oil-importing countries were facing the worst of the energy shock, and had difficult choices in helping their citizens through the crisis. “Unfortunately, after years of the global economy being hit [by] shock after shock, debt levels have increased quite a lot, and at the same time, inflation has become a problem,” she said. The US war on Iran has plunged the Middle East into conflict and sent global energy prices soaring , as Tehran’s retaliatory action targeted Washington’s Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies. Those prices have begun to bleed into other goods, with the crisis also having an effect on crucial fertiliser supplies. The IMF has called on countries to offer narrow, targeted subsidies in the wake of the crisis, while also recommending all governments work to rebuild fiscal buffers and address rising debt after years of fighting economic shocks since the pandemic. “Our messages indeed apply to most countries, but again, the trade-offs and the choices that have to be made are much more difficult for the most vulnerable countries,” Koeva Brooks said. The IMF’s World Economic Outlook , released on Tuesday, identified low-income developing countries that are net oil importers and are not exposed to the ongoing artificial intelligence technology investment boom as being the most vulnerable to the shocks from the Iran war. “For those countries that are most vulnerable, this is where the consumption basket is heavily weighted towards energy and food, and so indeed it is much much more difficult,” she said. “But unfortunately there is no other choice.” The senior IMF official added that “many” low-income countries were in debt distress, or close to it, and that they should seek debt restructuring if they were not able to address the issue. “Where debt is not sustainable, then resolving that debt and having orderly and timely restructuring is always better than waiting, because then the cost of restructuring down the road is going to be much higher,” she said. ‘Domino effect’ In its World Economic Outlook, the IMF raised its forecast for 2026 global growth, largely on the back of advanced economies enjoying a boost from AI-related investments and economic activity. Growth outcomes were highly uneven across economies, depending on their exposure to the war and whether they were integrated into AI supply chains. The world’s advanced economies were forecast to grow 2.1 per cent in 2026, with those in the AI supply chain such as Taiwan and South Korea posting significantly higher figures. Koeva Brooks told AFP that if AI investment activity were to slow, the world economy “would see a negative impact on output, not only in advanced countries like the US but again through trade linkages also in Asia”. In the IMF’s worst-case scenario — of AI not delivering promised productivity gains — global GDP forecasts for 2028 would fall by as much as 0.4pc. Climate-related risks were another key part of the World Economic Outlook this year, and Koeva Brooks told AFP that some of the effects of a particularly intense El Niño phenomenon had already been taken into account in higher prices for certain food items. The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Niño raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming. “We have a significant increase in beverage prices, in the prices of rice, and so on,” said Koeva Brooks. “Of course, it could turn out that the domino effect is even bigger than what we currently have.”

items.title: Burkina Faso : Des individus interpellés après avoir appelé à détruire des églises et des mosquées
items.description: Plusieurs individus se présentant comme des défenseurs des religions traditionnelles ont été interpellés au Burkina Faso après la diffusion d’une vidéo dans laquelle ils appelaient à se débarrasser des églises et des mosquées. L’information a été rapportée par l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB), ce mardi 13 octobre 2026. Selon l’AIB, les personnes interpellées devraient, dans un premier temps, effectuer des travaux d’intérêt commun hors de Ouagadougou, avant de faire face aux dispositions légales relatives aux libertés religieuses. La législation burkinabè en la matière garantit la liberté de croire ou de ne pas croire, interdit toute discrimination fondée sur la religion et prévoit des sanctions contre les discours de haine. Les auteurs de tels discours sont passibles de peines pouvant aller jusqu’à cinq ans d’emprisonnement, selon les dispositions évoquées par l’agence. Cette interpellation intervient dans un contexte où la préservation de la coexistence pacifique entre les différentes communautés religieuses constitue un enjeu majeur pour le Burkina Faso. items.title: The EU and the Internal Defence Market: What Are the National Perspectives?
items.description: À télécharger ARES Group #138 – Policy paper (PDF) Since the European Commission announced its intention to revive the project of an internal market for defence, Member States have been on alert. The issue is particularly sensitive. Using the EU budget to strengthen the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base (EDTIB) is one thing, regulating defence markets — and public procurement in particular — is quite another. Some countries are supportive, others remain sceptical, while others are still weighing up what position to take. The idea of an internal market for defence does, after all, raise major issues. This is no longer simply a matter of supporting industry: it touches on the very exercise of national sovereignty, as governments decide which weapons and military equipment their security will ultimately depend on. These questions have therefore been the subject of intense debate within the EU institutions for several months. In Brussels, even the terminology remains contested: a Defence Single Market? An Internal Market for Defence? A Defence Equipment Market? But what is the view from European capitals? How are these issues perceived at national level? And what positions do the main Member States intend to defend in Brussels? To answer these questions, the ARES Group asked nine of its researchers, based in nine EU capitals, to examine the debate from their respective national perspectives. The picture that emerges is a nuanced one. National positions certainly diverge, but they are far from set in stone, and several areas of convergence are beginning to emerge. More importantly, some of these disagreements appear to stem from misunderstandings that could be clarified, potentially opening the way to compromise. REMINDER: THE CHALLENGE FACING THE INTERNAL DEFENCE MARKET Analysing national perspectives DENMARK FRANCE GERMANY ITALY LITHUANIA POLAND SPAIN SWEDEN THE NETHERLANDS Conclusion CONCLUSION: DIVERGENCES ET CONVERGENCES L’article The EU and the Internal Defence Market: What Are the National Perspectives? est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Blé tendre : l’Algérie et la crise en mer Noire font remonter les prix
items.description: Les prix du blé tendre ont augmenté sur le marché mondial, poussés vers le haut par l’appel d'offres lancé par l’Algérie dimanche pour l’achat de 50 000 tonnes de blé, alors que sévit la crise en mer Noire où transitent les blés russes et ukrainiens. Dimanche, l’Office algérien des céréales (OAIC) a lancé un appel d’offres pour l’importation de 50 000 tonnes de blé tendre, un mois après avoir passé commande de 500 000 tonnes pour un tarif compris entre 319 et 321 dollars la tonne. Depuis, les prix du blé ont perdu du terrain, après que la Russie a trouvé une voie alternative pour écouler son blé via la Baltique. Blé tendre : les prix remontent à 271,37 dollars Dans ce contexte, et comme l’OAIC a pris l’habitude d’acheter une quantité plus importante que celle mentionnée dans l’appel d’offres, la nouvelle commande algérienne a provoqué une reprise du marché et une hausse des cours du blé européen de 0,5% à 271,37 dollars la tonne, rapportent plusieurs médias économiques. En plus de l’appel d’offres algérien, les prix du blé ont repris l’ascenseur après l’amenuisement des chances de progrès vers un accord de paix en mer Noire, qui permettrait à la Russie et à l’Ukraine, deux grands producteurs mondiaux de blé, d’écouler leurs récoltes par voie maritime. Avec 8,5 millions de tonnes d’importations prévues durant la campagne 2026-2027, l’Algérie fait partie des trois grands importateurs de blé au monde, après l’Égypte (13,5 millions de tonnes, 120 millions d’habitants) et l’Indonésie (12,5 millions de tonnes, 288 millions d’habitants). Proportionnellement à sa population, l’Algérie avec 48 millions d’habitants dépasse largement ces deux pays. items.title: RDC : l’ancien président Joseph Kabila, sous le coup d’une peine de mort pour trahison, et le groupe M23 s’unissent dans un mouvement politico-militaire
items.description: L’annonce d’une union entre Joseph Kabila et le M23 intervient dans un contexte politique incertain en RDC. Le président Félix Tshisekedi, 63 ans et successeur de Joseph Kabila, arrive au terme de son second et dernier mandat de cinq ans en 2028. L'ex-président de la RDC, Joseph Kabila , aujourd'hui opposant sous le coup d'une peine de mort pour trahison, est désormais à la tête d'un nouveau mouvement politico-militaire qui inclut le M23, confirmant ainsi ses liens avec le groupe armé antigouvernemental qui contrôle de vastes pans de territoire dans l'est du pays. L'annonce surprise, lundi soir, d'une union entre Joseph Kabila et le M23 soutenu par le Rwanda, intervient dans un contexte politique incertain en République démocratique du Congo (RDC), pays d'Afrique centrale à l'histoire politique agitée. L'actuel président Félix Tshisekedi , 63 ans et successeur de Joseph Kabila, arrive au terme de son second et dernier mandat de cinq ans en 2028. La Constitution congolaise place la limite à deux quinquennats. Or, depuis déjà plusieurs mois, la majorité présidentielle prépare l'opinion à l'idée d'une modification constitutionnelle ou d'un changement de Constitution, ouvrant potentiellement la voie à un troisième mandat pour Félix Tshisekedi. Des manifestations émaillées de heurts L'opposition, qui accuse le président de manœuvres visant à se maintenir au pouvoir mais peine à susciter un soutien populaire, a organisé des rassemblements de contestation en juin et en septembre. Ces manifestations dans la capitale Kinshasa et plusieurs autres grandes villes du pays ont été souvent émaillées de heurts et quasi systématiquement dispersées par les forces de l'ordre. Les Nations Unies ont déploré «au moins un mort» lors du premier rassemblement à Kinshasa et «l'assassinat» d'un opposant a été dénoncé par l'opposition lors du second. Joseph Kabila, dont les apparitions publiques sont rares et qui garde généralement le plus grand secret sur ses déplacements, est apparu lundi devant la presse, au côté de plusieurs hauts responsables du M23. Il n'a pas pris la parole. L'ancien président (2001-2019) avait lui-même tenté de prolonger son règne au-delà de deux mandats en modifiant la loi électorale. La pression de la rue et de la communauté internationale l'avaient finalement contraint à renoncer. La répression de manifestations anti-Kabila avait fait des dizaines de morts. «La dictature doit prendre fin en RDC» L'annonce de la création du mouvement baptisé Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), présidé par Joseph Kabila, a été faite depuis la résidence de ce dernier à Goma, grande ville de l'est contrôlée par le M23. Les hauts responsables du M23 et de l'Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), ancienne branche politique du groupe armé désormais dissoute avec la création du FRN, occupent des postes de vice-présidents. Les membres du FRN se sont unis pour «mutualiser leurs forces, ressources et moyens» avec pour objectif de «mettre un terme à la tyrannie par tous les moyens y compris la force» en RDC, ont-ils expliqué dans une déclaration politique. Le M23 a plusieurs fois clamé sa volonté de renverser le président Tshisekedi. De son côté, Joseph Kabila a déclaré dans une allocution en ligne en mai 2025 que «la dictature doit prendre fin en RDC» . Il avait ajouté qu'il était prêt à «jouer sa partition» . Après avoir quitté le pays pendant plusieurs années, il était réapparu à Goma quelques jours après ce discours. Ce retour au pays avait inquiété Kinshasa dans un contexte d'instabilité liée à l'intensification du conflit dans l'est du pays début 2025. Sur injonction du gouvernement, son immunité parlementaire avait été levée et un procès organisé en son absence s'était soldé fin septembre par une condamnation à la peine capitale pour trahison et crime de guerre. La justice militaire avait jugé que Joseph Kabila était l'un des initiateurs de l'AFC. L'est congolais est en proie à des violences depuis plus de 30 ans. Au terme d'une offensive spectaculaire en janvier et février 2025, le M23 soutenu par l'armée rwandaise s'est emparé des deux grandes villes de Goma et Bukavu, face à des forces armées congolaises dépassées. Plusieurs tentatives de médiations pour rétablir la paix dans la région ont échoué jusqu'ici. Un accord signé en décembre par Kinshasa et Kigali, sous l'égide de Washington, n'a pas eu d'effet concret sur le terrain. Parallèlement, Kinshasa et le M23 se sont engagés en juillet 2025, dans le cadre d'une médiation qatarie, à un cessez-le-feu, qui n'est pas respecté. Avec AFP L’article RDC : l’ancien président Joseph Kabila, sous le coup d’une peine de mort pour trahison, et le groupe M23 s’unissent dans un mouvement politico-militaire est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: IMF upgrades forecast for Nigeria’s economic growth to 4.2%
items.description: *Warns of tougher times as global growth slows to 3.1% *Says AI boom, energy shocks threaten global economic outlook By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has upgraded its forecast for Nigeria’s economic growth for 2026 to 4.2 per cent but warned that rising energy and food prices, geopolitical tensions and potential market corrections linked to artificial intelligence (AI) threaten the global economic outlook. The new forecast was contained in the IMF World Economic Outlook report October 2026, titled Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices”, released on Monday during the ongoing annual meetings of the IMF/World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand. Furthermore, the new forecast represents one percentage point above the 4.1 per cent earlier projected by the IMF in the July 2026 edition of its WEO. According to the IMF, “Growth in sub-Saharan Africa is expected to remain stable at 4.5 per cent in 2026, though this masks substantial divergence across countries, reflecting differences in policy space, reform implementation, commodity exposure, climate shocks, and access to external financing. “Oil-importing, non-resource-intensive economies are more adversely affected by higher energy and food prices, whereas some larger economies continue to benefit from earlier stabilisation and reform efforts, even though they are largely absent from the AI-driven global technology upswing and face headwinds from declines in official development assistance. “Nigeria is supported by improved macroeconomic stability and favourable terms-of-trade effects, though higher prices for essentials are expected to further aggravate poverty and food insecurity.” Global growth under pressure However, the IMF warned that the global economy’s resilience was under increasing pressure, with growth projected to slow from 3.5 per cent in 2025 to 3.1 per cent in 2026, before recovering to 3.4 per cent in 2027. Speaking at the press briefing on the WEO report, Sylvana Tenreyro, the IMF’s Economic Counsellor and Director of the Research Department, said, “The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is under strain, with risks tilted to the downside.” She added, “The task ahead is to move from coping to rebuilding,” stressing the need to restore fiscal space, strengthen supply-side resilience and improve countries’ capacity to withstand future economic shocks. Explaining the global outlook, Tenreyro identified energy and commodity price increases as major factors weighing on economic activity, while investment associated with artificial intelligence had provided support for growth.” The IMF report noted that the global economy had withstood repeated shocks, including geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions, but cautioned that “these margins of adjustment are not unlimited.” According to the IMF, the interaction between geopolitical tensions and technological investment has created divergent growth outcomes across countries. While economies benefiting from technology-related investment and favourable commodity trade conditions have received some support, others face higher import bills, exchange-rate pressures and weaker real incomes. The Fund warned that prolonged geopolitical tensions could keep energy and food prices elevated, revive inflationary pressures, worsen fiscal and external balances, and weigh on economic growth. Global headline inflation is projected to rise from 4.1 per cent in 2025 to 4.7 per cent in 2026 before easing to 4.1 per cent in 2027, with higher energy and food prices driving the temporary increase. AI boom raises fresh risks The IMF also cautioned that the technology investment boom, particularly in artificial intelligence, could become a source of financial instability. Although AI-related investment has supported economic activity and international trade, the Fund warned that investment gains were concentrated in a relatively small number of firms, sectors and economies. It cautioned that “a reassessment of AI-related profitability and productivity prospects could sharply reduce investment, trigger equity market corrections, and tighten financial conditions.” Such a correction, the report said, could spill over into economies integrated into technology supply chains and markets with significant exposure to technology stocks. Urges fiscal discipline Against this backdrop, Tenreyro called on governments to rebuild fiscal buffers, safeguard financial stability and strengthen private-sector dynamism. “Fiscal policy must be restrained and help contain demand pressures at a time of heightened inflationary risks,” the IMF chief economist said in the report. The Fund also stressed the importance of monetary policy focused on price stability, adding that “central bank independence is instrumental in achieving that goal.” “The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits,” urging countries to strengthen their capacity to withstand future disruptions and achieve sustainable growth,” Tenreyro added. items.title: Govt says people of KP ‘welcomed’ governor's rule as it gave them ‘hope’
items.description: Information Minister Ataullah Tarar on Tuesday claimed that the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had “welcomed” the federal government’s move to impose governor’s rule and emergency in the province, saying the measures had given them “hope”. The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency in 12 districts of KP, and placed the province under governor’s rule, taking note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”. He made the remarks while addressing a press conference alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar. Ataullah noted, “Had the people of KP supported the pro-terrorist stance of the PTI government, you would have seen millions on the street.” The minister went on to claim that “barely a dozen” people had gathered in protest. Defending the move, the information minister said: “The people of KP have welcomed the step because they believe there is now hope for them. They believe they will now be provided with safety and security, their lives and livelihoods will be protected, and this political-crime nexus will be eliminated.” At the outset of the press briefing, the law minister noted that the province in the recent past had witnessed a hike in terrorist incidents, noting a “195 per cent” rise, with 8,600 terrorist attacks recorded in 2024-2026 compared to 2,900 in 2020-2024. Azam emphasised that it was essential that counterterrorism efforts taken by federal and provincial agencies be “harmonised”, adding that such an approach was standard practice globally. “All these arrangements are made to run the country in a way that people feel safe,” he remarked. At this, the law minister noted the “non-serious” attitude of the previous PTI-led KP government, which he said, “has now ceased to exist”. He recalled that the PTI, allegedly using government resources, “launched an onslaught on the capital”. However, at the time, the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency did not come under discussion. Describing the situation on the ground in the province, the law minister said: “The KP police were under attack, armed forces deployed in the province were under attack […] innocent people lost their lives.” “You cannot shut your eyes after receiving such reports and seeing this rise in terrorist activity,” Azam added. Recalling the events leading up to the federal government’s decision, Azam said the government had held “constant engagement” with the provincial authorities. “Unfortunately, their response was somewhat different. Maybe their politics were more important to them than having the national interest at heart,” he said. He maintained that the federal government had exhausted “all possible avenues” to resolve the differences. Azam said the provincial government should have intervened amid “internal disturbances or the likelihood or apprehension of such disturbances”. Referring to Article 232, under which the emergency was imposed, Azam said it “deals with internal disturbances where the law and order situation is such, and the onslaught is of a nature that the provincial government cannot fight against it”. Referring to the PTI, he said, “Your priorities were not to curb terrorism or to fight against it”. “In such grave conditions, your priority should be to protect the people, not to pursue political gains.” Azam said it was against this backdrop that the prime minister brought the matter before the federal cabinet, and a decision was subsequently made. On being asked why similar measures could not be enacted in Balochistan, despite the prevailing security situation in the province, Azam said: “Look at the conduct of the Balochistan government; the chief minister is on his toes [..] he is trying hard.” He noted that whenever there is a terrorist incident in Balochistan, the CM visits the area himself and personally oversees relief efforts. ‘Total breakdown of governance’ Ataullah, during the presser, reiterated that the federal government did not have a political agenda against the PTI-led provincial government; instead, it was pursuing “a unified policy on counterterrorism”. “You cannot have a government in the country that sympathises with terrorists, supports terrorism or has a policy that enables terrorists to carry out their operational actions,” he said. He questioned how one country could have two separate counterterrorism policies. “As the [law] minister explained, the framers of the constitution included these clauses (232 and 234) for a time like this,” citing a “complete breakdown” of law and order in KP. He further went on to question why resources allocated to the provincial government via the National Finance Commission were not utilised to strengthen security-related infrastructure and equip KP police. The information minister reiterated that the PTI-led government was facilitating the terrorists, describing it as a “political-terrorist nexus”. He further said there was a “total breakdown of governance” in KP, noting a lack of reforms in education, health, and public services. Sunday’s directives came after a meeting of the federal cabinet deliberated on the security situation in PTI-led KP. During the meeting, the cabinet noted the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”. Subsequently, the federal government imposed emergency under Article 232 and governor’s rule under Article 234. Soon after, it also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in the province. On the ground, shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block several roads, with heavy police deployment. Meanwhile, federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, as the Centre sought to explain that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there. A day earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the move, saying it was not politically motivated but instead taken to curb terrorism. The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their October 3 talks . The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations. On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

items.title: Acte V : la colère lycéenne pourrait s’élargir aux étudiants et au mouvement social
items.description: Alors que le ministre de l'education nationale edouard Geffray anticipe une baisse des blocages avec environ 200 lycees fermes sur 3 700, les organisateurs misent sur un elargissement. MARDI 13 OCTOBRE : MANIFESTATION ÉTUDIANTE & LYCÉENNE : NOUVEL ACTE. 14H DÉPART DE LA PLACE D'ITALIE. https://t.co/0dw1ktH80g — L’Union Étudiante (@unionetudiante_) October 9, 2026 a Paris, le cortege lyceen et etudiant partira a 14 heures de la place d'Italie vers les Invalides. Des rassemblements sont aussi prevus a Lyon, Marseille, Lille, Toulouse et Bordeaux. Des revendications inchangees face aux reponses jugees insuffisantes Demarre a la mi-septembre, le mouvement denonce le manque de moyens, les professeurs non remplaces, les bâtiments delabres, les emplois du temps surcharges et la pression de Parcoursup. L'Union syndicale lyceenne exige toujours la suppression de cette plateforme et un plan de dix milliards d'euros. Les annonces gouvernementales – deploiement de 3 000 professeurs remplacants, dont 35 % deja affectes selon Geffray, et des amendements budgetaires – ne satisfont pas les organisations de gauche. Des personnels de l'education nationale et de l'enseignement superieur rejoignent la contestation. Une dizaine de syndicats reclament de meilleurs salaires, l'annulation de suppressions de postes et la levee des barrages de Parcoursup et Mon Master. Des blocages d'universites, comme a Paris-Pantheon-Assas, symbolisent deja cette jonction. Sur place, plusieurs elus de La France insoumise (LFI) sont venus apporter leur soutien aux bloqueurs, notamment Aurelien Saintoul, Thomas Portes et Ersilia Soudais. Ce matin, la faculté d’Assas est bloquée par plus d’une centaine de personnes, beaucoup masquées. Parfois, ils scandent «Acab !» ou «À bas l’État policier !». Dans la foule, avec leur écharpe tricolore, les députés LFI Aurélien Saintoul, Thomas Portes et Ersilia Soudais. https://t.co/XRyYLW8Jia — Jean-Baptiste Semerdjian (@JBSemerdjian) October 13, 2026 Le gouvernement constate une deceleration : lundi, 96,5 % des etablissements etaient ouverts, avec 130 fermes contre 172 vendredi. « On est plutot sur une decrue par rapport aux semaines precedentes », a declare Geffray sur France Inter. Le president de la Republique Emmanuel Macron a, lui, appele a manifester « dans le calme, dans l'ordre et dans le respect ». De leur cote, les organisateurs visent la convergence avec la mobilisation « contre la vie chere » prevue le 17 octobre, premier jour des vacances de la Toussaint. Entre 130 000 et 200 000 personnes sont attendues dans les rues ce 13 octobre, dans ce qui pourrait faire figure de prelude a la journee du 17.
