items.title: Türkiye: COP31 Host Curbs Environment Defenders
items.description: Click to expand Image Local residents of Perşembe Plateau and representatives of environmental organizations stage a protest against gold mining exploration in the area, July 19, 2026. © 2026 Private (Istanbul, October 13, 2026) – The authorities in Türkiye, the host of the upcoming 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), are arbitrarily arresting and prosecuting activists and others involved in environmental protests even as the summit nears, Human Rights Watch said today. “With Türkiye about to host the annual UN climate change summit, its environmental crackdown is a salient reminder of its intolerance of dissent,” said Deniz Bayram, assistant Europe and Central Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Turkish authorities should listen to people’s concerns about the environmental impact of activities such as mining in their areas and address them, instead of arresting and prosecuting protesters.” In August 2026, Human Rights Watch interviewed 23 people who had been at environmental protests and reviewed relevant media reports, documents, and judicial proceedings. Human Rights Watch also documented the treatment of environmental protesters in two of the areas currently affected. Protests against coal mining in the Akbelen forest in Türkiye’s southwest Muğla province have been taking place since 2023, while gold mining exploration in the Perşembe Plateau and surrounding areas in the eastern Black Sea region has sparked protests throughout 2026. Authorities in both areas have forcibly dispersed nonviolent protesters, including by using tear gas, water cannons, and pepper spray. Police have arrested and fined protesters and intimidated local residents with arbitrary identity checks. In September, Human Rights Watch wrote to the Interior Ministry, the Milas Chief Prosecution Office in Muğla, the Korgan Chief Prosecution Office in Ordu, and the Tirebolu Chief Prosecution Office in Giresun seeking further information and a response to the findings. None have responded at the time of writing. Law enforcement and security forces have arrested community members, lawyers, and journalists at protests. Protesters face a variety of criminal charges and investigations on dubious allegations including illegal gathering, using violence to prevent a public official from carrying out their duty, trespassing, insulting public officials, and spreading false information. The authorities have also temporarily arrested at least two people who expressed support for the protests online. In one instance, on July 29, the authorities arrested protesters in the eastern Black Sea area for up to eight hours without legal due process. Those arrested included two children and an 84-year-old woman. Environmental defenders have also faced criminal charges, administrative fines, and other legal pressure for monitoring environmental harm or seeking to protect their land and environment. In advance of a July NATO summit in Ankara, the authorities ordered the arrest of 225 people, ranging from political activists to nature conservation supporters, on suspicion of “membership in armed organizations.” Courts on June 25 and 26 placed 178 in pretrial detention and 34 under judicial control, without citing compelling evidence of criminal activity. Among those detained were 13 members of a nature conservation organization who were later released, along with 14 others who had been under house arrest. The continuing criminal investigations and arrests of environmental protestors since 2023 have created a significant chilling effect on the rights to expression and assembly, protected under international human rights law and the Turkish constitution. Many have ended in decisions not to prosecute or acquittals, but investigations impose an immense burden on those targeted, as they last for years and require them to appear repeatedly before law enforcement agencies. A 75-year-old woman in Denizli, in western Türkiye, was fined in May 2024 when she refused to allow two mining company staff access to her property in a protest against coal mining. She was accused of beating the staff members, allegations she strenuously denies. The decision is under appeal. Police and gendarmes have prevented journalists and bystanders from filming environmental protests in the affected areas, in some cases using violence, and arrested and opened investigations against journalists covering the protests, media reported. Human Rights Watch has previously raised concerns with Turkish authorities that its efforts to expand coal mining and coal-fired power capacity in Türkiye pose serious risks to public health, environmental protection, and the protection of other human rights. The crackdown on environmental defenders is part of a wider attack on civic space in the country, Human Rights Watch said, including the detention of activists in Istanbul protesting an anti-LGBT crackdown on September 15, 2026. Some of them allege that they were ill-treated during the more than 24 hours they were arrested. Civil society participation is important for holding states to account for their environmental policies, Human Rights Watch said. It is also essential in contexts where decisions made by the central government can have serious local environmental impact. As host of COP31 in November, Türkiye has an obligation to facilitate the participation of civil society in the conference. “The Turkish government has ignored environmental protections and turned on local people who are speaking out against environmental damage to their communities,” Bayram said. “States attending COP31 should speak out against Türkiye’s crackdown on environmental defenders and remind their hosts that civil society participation is critical to achieving COP goals.” For additional details, please see below. Methodology In August 2026, Human Rights Watch interviewed 23 people who had been at environmental protests: 15 community members, 6 lawyers, and 2 journalists. Human Rights Watch documented investigations and prosecutions related to long-running environmental protests in Akbelen forest in Muğla, western Türkiye, between 2023 and 2026, and protests in the eastern Black Sea region in 2026, as well as investigations linked to those protests. Human Rights Watch also reviewed media reports, indictments, traffic penalties, and other administrative fines issued against protesters; court decisions, court-appointed expert reports relevant to the protests, and forensic medical reports; and photographs from protesters documenting their injuries. Human Rights Watch examined the judicial proceedings against protesters in four cases in İkizköy village, in the Milas district of Türkiye’s southwestern Muğla province, including relevant investigation documents and the decisions on conviction and acquittal, and assessed the laws used to prosecute them. Akbelen: Protests Banned Over Coal Mining in Forest, Olive Groves Click to expand Image Since 2023, local residents have been protesting forest clearance for coal mining, İkizköy, Muğla, Türkiye, August‎ ‎6‎, ‎2023. © 2023 Kazım Kızıl Since 2019, residents of İkizköy have been pursuing court cases to prevent the expansion of an open-pit lignite mine into Akbelen forest, the clearance of the legally protected forest, and the expropriation of nearby olive groves. The forest clearing case is pending while a court halted the expropriation of the olive groves. On July 17, 2021, after the Muğla Forestry Directorate cut down about 30 trees, community members began to monitor Akbelen forest for potential unlawful activity. On August 10, about 250 gendarmes intervened and arrested 11 protesters, including Füsun Ergün, who was forcibly removed after tying herself to an olive tree. Ergün and another environment defender, Gülören Demir, were convicted of resisting public officials and sentenced to 6 months and 20 days in prison, subsequently converted to fines. Click to expand Image During protests, the gendarmerie intervened with riot shields and water cannon against demonstrators, July, 28, 2026, İkizköy, Muğla, Türkiye. © 2026 Kazım Kızıl When the authorities resumed clearing the forest in July 2023, police used tear gas and water cannons against protesting villagers. The media reported that at least 40 people were arrested, including 14 later charged with resisting police officers. A broad coalition of civil society groups from across the country soon joined the protests. By August 2023, the authorities had cut down about three-fifths of the forest, despite the pending court case. Click to expand Image Despite pending court cases challenging the forest clearance and urgent expropriation, large areas of Akbelen Forest have already been cut down, İkizköy, Muğla, Türkiye, July 30, 2023. © 2023 Kazım Kızıl The government has prosecuted six community members for their participation or presence at various protests since 2023. Four were convicted for resisting public officials and are appealing. Two of them, Ahmet Tatar, 63, who faced multiple charges of resisting public officials, and an 85-year-old man accused of insulting the president, were acquitted. At least 55 others have been criminally investigated, 3 lawyers representing community members said. Many of the investigations have remained open for years. İsmail Atal, a lawyer who is himself the subject of two investigations, said that “keeping the investigations [open] for years leaves the threat of prosecution hanging over protesters like a Sword of Damocles, deterring them from taking part in further protests.” The Human Rights Watch review of the cases and interviews with those investigated suggests a pattern of intimidation aimed at discouraging protests. The authorities have arrested Tatar three times, and he said prosecutors had opened ten criminal investigations against him, most for allegedly resisting public officials or preventing them from performing their duties. Eight are ongoing, and two resulted in prosecutions both ending in acquittals. The prosecutor appealed the acquittals, and to date one acquittal has been upheld. “Of course I will continue to join protests,” Tatar said. “It is my moral obligation to humanity. But it is difficult and burdensome to deal with all these investigations.” Prosecutors have, however, failed to effectively investigate allegations against security officers for violations of protesters’ rights in Akbelen. On September 13, 2023, Tatar said, gendarmes broke his camera, struck him with their hands on his back and ankles, forced him face-down to the ground, pressed on his neck and back, cuffed his hands behind his back, and searched his tent. Tatar said he identified the gendarmes by name and filed complaints, supported by medical reports documenting his injuries, but the court dismissed his complaints. İpek Sarica, another lawyer, also filed a criminal complaint about violence she says she experienced during a protest in 2023. After a prosecutor declined to prosecute the case, Sarica appealed, but her complaint has remained unresolved for over three years. In a third case, Nejla Işık, the village head of İkizköy, filed a complaint alleging a violation of her right to privacy after a siginal jammer and a large number of gendarmes were deployed very close to her house. Prosecutors declined to open a case, which Işık’s lawyers challenged. The case is pending before the Constitutional Court. Güven Göknar, 66, from Muğla, said he intervened in a July 2023 protest against deforestation when gendarmes used pepper spray against protesters at close range. He was sentenced to five months in prison for allegedly resisting public officials, after footage showing him raising his hand was misinterpreted as showing him throwing a stone. He said he raised his hand to tell the gendarmes to stop; his appeal is pending. On March 30, 2026, Esra Işık, 26, was arrested during a protest against an expropriation order covering 649 land parcels in İkizköy. She spent 42 days in pretrial detention. On July 6, the Milas Criminal Court convicted her of “resisting officials” and sentenced her to two years and one month in prison, together with a suspended sentence for insulting public officials. Esra Işık’s lawyers have appealed. Another lawyer interviewed said that community members have been fined between 40,000 to 250,000 Turkish lira (about US$825 to $5,160) for acts including putting up tents and banners in connection with the Akbelen protests. People who have been fined and their lawyers said that in some cases fines were finalized without proper notification, with officials falsely recording that recipients had refused to accept notifications being served. As a result, some community members faced seizures of their bank accounts and property, while some were forced to pay. A lawyer said they had succeeded in having some fines cancelled, but not all of them. In 2023, prosecutors investigated 25 environmental activists in Edremit, on the north Aegean coast, for an unauthorized protest in solidarity with environment defenders in Akbelen. The case was later dropped. The authorities have also exerted pressure on lawyers representing the Akbelen community. Atal said that gendarmes arrested him on allegations of obstructing public officials as he traveled to the village on July 29, 2023, held him for several hours, and that he has been kept under investigation. Prosecutors opened a criminal investigation against Arif Ali Cangı, another lawyer, for allegedly inciting hatred and hostility among the public after he posted a social media post criticizing continued mining activity in Akbelen in the aftermath of the 2023 earthquake. The investigation remains open. The experience of journalists covering environmental protests suggests that the authorities open criminal investigations deliberately to interfere with their work. Prosecutors summoned a citizen journalist, Zeynep Kuray, on August 3, 2023, while she was reporting on the Akbelen protests. She then learned that the Milas Prosecution Office had opened an investigation against her for “spreading misleading information,” a criminal offense punishable with a prison term of one to three years, which eventually closed in 2024. Two other journalists arrested at their homes in İzmir in February 2024 said that police had questioned them about their presence at the Akbelen protests. Eastern Black Sea: Crackdown against Gold Mining Protests In Türkiye’s eastern Black Sea region, residents of the Perşembe Plateau have been protesting gold mining exploration since early 2026. The high plateau is in the northern part of Korgan-Aybastı districts, about 110 kilometers from Ordu, the provincial capital. The residents raise livestock for their livelihoods. The area designated for gold exploration is classified as pasture under Turkish law and requires specific permits to be mined. Türkiye’s Environment Ministry issued a permit in 2024. Human Rights Watch interviewed 11 residents who said they had been excluded from consultation and information about the project, which could potentially force them to relocate. They became aware of the project after it began affecting water they needed for livestock and household use, as well as from public statements by environmental groups. The community challenged the Environment Ministry’s permit. A court-assigned expert report dated June 15, 2026, warned that the project could disrupt the area’s hydrogeology, or groundwater flow, and that local water resources were critical to pastoral activities, livestock farming, and the community’s drinking and domestic water needs. Click to expand Image Local residents of Perşembe Plateau, together with the Ordu Environmental Organization, gathered to make a press statement opposing the gold exploration project, July 19, 2026, Korgan, Ordu. © 2026 Private The authorities fined the protesting community members in June and August in Giresun and Ordu provinces for hanging banners and issued traffic penalties for alleged “improper parking,” which residents believe was retaliation for protesting. On July 29, more than 50 residents protested drilling in Perşembe Plateau. Gendarmes arrested about 15 people. Human Rights Watch interviewed four men who were among at least 11 taken to the Tepealan gendarmerie station in Korgan, some handcuffed. They said they were held for about eight hours without being told why or whether they were under investigation, then released. One said gendarmes made some arrestees sign a document stating that they would not attend any further protests. The men said they have received no information since about any investigation or legal basis for their arrest. Leyla Acerce, 40, attended the protest with her husband and four children. She said that gendarmes formed a large circle, their shields pointing outwards, and pushed her into the circle, where she fainted. She was dragged and left sitting in a chair outside in heavy rain for hours. She was later transferred alone to Korgan State Hospital by ambulance. Acerce said she called the police from the hospital to report that she had been beaten by the gendarmes. The police came to the hospital. The hospital gave the police the medical report documenting her injuries but refused her a copy. Her husband, Ali Acerce, 47, said that when he tried to help his wife, three gendarmes handcuffed him, twisted his arm, and forced him into a container, where he was held for about two hours. He was then taken to the Tepealan gendarmerie station, where he was held for six hours and then released. He said that their 22-year-old son, İlyas, was also arrested for about six hours. Police made the family wait for hours when they went to the police station to file a complaint about their treatment by the gendarmes. They are not aware of any action on their complaint. Nuriye Dilek, 48, and another woman in her 50s who requested anonymity out of fear for her family, said four gendarmes dragged them from the protest and forced them into an unmarked white van. “They threw me into the van like a sack,” Dilek said.” I thought they would break our arms as they twisted them.” Human Rights Watch observed bruising on Dilek’s wrists and on the other woman’s chest and arms six days after the protest. Interviewees also said that they saw gendarmes drag two girls, both under 18, by their hair and put them into an unmarked van. Dilek said she saw gendarmes and plain clothes officers pointing out community members who had spoken out about defending the plateau in videos shared on social media. Musa Duman, 60, said that during questioning in a separate investigation, a prosecutor asked him about photos and videos he had shared online from the protests. Click to expand Image Gendarmerie block local residents from Perşembe Plateau from reaching the gold mining drilling site to stage a protest, July 16, 2026. © 2026 Private Residents said that after the protest, they faced a range of apparent retaliatory measures by the gendarmerie, including repeated identity checks in the small community where they had lived for years. If they did not carry identification, gendarmes photographed their faces at close range “as if we were criminals,” one resident said. Residents also reported verbal harassment and that following a solidarity protest on August 1, 17 traffic fines were issued to protesters and visitors for alleged improper parking or tinted windows. Local activists also said gendarmes used a signal jammer during the protest to disrupt communications, and Human Rights Watch reviewed photographs showing gendarmes carrying jamming equipment. Jammers were also used at other protests in Akbelen. An 84-year-old woman who had been arrested said she was now hesitant to appear in protest photos or videos after gendarmes contacted her sons, who live in other cities, and told them not to let their mother attend protests. Dilek also said that authorities had contacted her son. Dilek said that her husband, Halil Dilek, 53, and another man were arrested on suspicion of theft of materials related to mining operations and detained overnight at the Tepealan gendarmerie station. Halil Dilek said that he was distressed because his wife was travelling and that his teenage daughter was alone at home. He said that the prosecutor who questioned him the following day asked about his participation in the protests and photos he had shared on social media, raising concerns of surveillance and pressure over his environmental activism. On August 27, residents of Perşembe Plateau, including Duman and Nuriye Dilek, met with Ordu’s governor to discuss the project and the excessive use of force and violence by the gendarmerie. When Dilek said that gendarmes had beaten and dragged her and that her clothes had been torn open during the altercation, she said the governor asked what she was doing there in the first place. Duman said that on September 9, gendarmes summoned him to give a statement about his Facebook post criticizing the governor’s response. He was told he was suspected of publicly disseminating misleading information. The authorities have sought to suppress environmental protests in other areas of the eastern Black Sea designated for gold mining exploration. On April 5, residents of Görele and Tirebolu in Giresun province, east of Ordu, gathered to protest work at a gold mining project, despite a court order suspending the work. A large number of gendarmes confronted them, said a lawyer, Sevda Karataş, and the company complained the protesters had interfered with its “freedom to work.” Subsequently, Karataş, Ömer Cebeci, a municipal council member, and Nihal Nakıpoğlu, a local environmental association member, were summoned for questioning by the prosecutor. Karataş, who represents two community members from Tirebolu in Giresun, said that a prosecutor investigated her clients for alleged threats, disseminating misleading information, and interfering with the company’s “freedom to work.” The investigation remains open. Mesut Yilmaz, a 33-year-old local resident who actively posts about the protests on social media, said that police questioned him for about six hours about more than 100 pages of his social media posts. On June 2, he was fined, paying the maximum penalty of 115,000 lira (about $2,500) for putting up banners announcing a gold mining protest for May 29. The Right to Protest Under Human Rights Law The right to peaceful protest is protected under international human rights law, including under the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) and International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR); Türkiye is party to both. The right to peaceful assembly is closely linked to the right to freedom of expression. While the rights to freedom of assembly and expression are not absolute and can be subject to restrictions, both the ECHR and ICCPR require that any restriction must be prescribed by law to pursue a legitimate aim and to be necessary and proportionate to that aim. Blanket bans on protests are disproportionate and unjustifiable. The UN Human Rights Committee, which oversees compliance with the ICCPR, in its General Comment No. 37 (2020) stipulates that peaceful assemblies should not be criminalized, and that states must facilitate and protect such gatherings. The European Court of Human Rights has repeatedly found that Turkish authorities’ use of powers under the Law on Meetings and Demonstrations (Law no. 2911) to ban or disperse protests and punish protestors violated the right of assembly. The right to peaceful protest is also protected under the article 34 of the Turkish constitution, which guarantees the right to organize peaceful, unarmed demonstrations and marches without prior permission.

items.title: Govt denies role as anchor­per­son Iqrarul Hassan ‘picked up’ in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: Anchor­per­son Iqrarul Hassan was allegedly picked up by men in plainclothes, one of whom was wearing an identification tag of the Natio­nal Cyber Crime Investi­gation Agency (NCCIA), from his residence in Lahore in the early hours of Monday, his family said. Punjab minister Azma Bokhari clarified police had not arrested Mr Hassan and the matter was being investigated. In a video, Far­ah Iqrar said she and her husband were at their residence in DHA when men in plainclothes broke open the main gate, entered the pre­mises at around 3am and took Mr Hassan away. She alleged that the men manhandled her during the operation and confiscated two mobile phones belonging to her husband, a laptop and her own mo­­bile phone. She added that a masked woman among the raiding party was wearing an NCCIA identification tag. Mr Hassan had been critical of the government’s policies on social media. Advocate Mian Ali Ashfaq, counsel for Mr Hassan, said the NCCIA had denied arresting him. He added that the anc­h­­or had not made any anti-state remarks. “We will move the Lahore High Court for his safe recovery,” he said. Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: Ouagadougou : Le Premier ministre inaugure le complexe scolaire de R+3 de plus d’un milliard de FCFA à Bonheur-Ville
items.description: Le Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a procédé, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, à l'inauguration officielle du complexe scolaire primaire public Faso-Kéoogo à Bonheur-Ville, dans le 7ᵉ arrondissement de Ouagadougou. Financé à hauteur de plus d'un milliard de francs CFA sur ressources propres de l'État dans le cadre de l'Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous (IPEQ), ce bâtiment pédagogique en R+3 accueille déjà 1 453 élèves répartis dans trois écoles. Incarnant la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, cet édifice moderne vise à optimiser l'espace urbain tout en offrant un cadre d'apprentissage d'excellence au cœur d'une zone en forte croissance démographique. C'est dans le 7ᵉ arrondissement de Ouagadougou que le gouvernement a concrétisé une promesse majeure en matière d'infrastructures scolaires. Ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, le Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a officiellement coupé le ruban inaugural du complexe scolaire public de Bonheur-Ville après le dévoilement de la plaque symbolique. Bâti sur une parcelle de 35 384 m² déclarée d'utilité publique d'urgence en mai 2024, ce bâtiment pédagogique en R+3 a nécessité un investissement de plus d'un milliard de francs CFA, intégralement financé par le budget national. L'édifice comprend 16 salles de classe, soit quatre par niveau, ainsi que des blocs sanitaires spécialement aménagés pour les personnes à mobilité réduite. Dès sa première année de fonctionnement (2026-2027), l'infrastructure regroupe trois écoles — Faso-Kéoogo-Bonheur-Ville C, D et E — comptabilisant 1 453 élèves, dont 742 filles, encadrés par 32 enseignants. Présent aux côtés du Chef du Gouvernement, le ministre de l'Enseignement de base, de l'Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des langues nationales, Jacques Sosthène Dingara, a souligné que cette réalisation matérialise la volonté du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, d'équiper le pays d'infrastructures modernes et adaptées aux besoins réels de la population. Pour le Premier ministre, cette infrastructure incarne l'ambition éducative de la Révolution progressiste populaire, se dressant comme un modèle d'école novateur capable d'optimiser l'espace au sol tout en améliorant la qualité des apprentissages. Il a rappelé que cette dynamique de modernisation globale touchera l'ensemble du système éducatif, du primaire au supérieur. Les leçons tirées de cette structure pilote permettront d'optimiser la construction de quinze autres complexes similaires prévus dans quinze provinces, lesquels adopteront des formats élargis à 18 salles de classe, avec des capacités d'extension allant jusqu'à 24 classes. Au-delà de sa dimension architecturale et fonctionnelle, l'établissement revêt une valeur morale et patriotique profonde à travers son appellation « Faso-Kéoogo ». Le Premier ministre a rappelé que le terme « Kéoogo » fait référence au traditionnel camp d'initiation, lieu sacré de transmission des savoirs et de préparation de la jeunesse aux responsabilités de la cité. Ainsi, l'école doit former des esprits brillants tout en inculquant le patriotisme, la dignité, la fierté nationale et la solidarité. En s'adressant directement aux jeunes élèves, le Chef du Gouvernement les a invités à la discipline, à l'assiduité et au respect strict de leurs installations. Un engagement pleinement partagé par le représentant du Conseil des écoles, Daouda Traoré, qui a exprimé la gratitude des parents et de la communauté, promettant de faire de ce complexe un creuset de vertus et un phare de savoir préservé pour les générations futures. items.title: Tragédie routière dans le Tuy : Un camion-benne s’encastre contre un arbre à Nématoulaye, faisant un mort et un blessé grave
items.description: Un tragique accident de la route s'est produit ce lundi 12 octobre 2026 aux environs de 13 heures à Nématoulaye, dans la commune de Houndé. Un camion-benne circulant sur la Route Nationale 1 (RN1) a quitté la chaussée avant d'aller percuter violemment un arbre. Le choc brutal a coûté la vie à l'apprenti-chauffeur sur les lieux du drame et grièvement blessé le conducteur, qui a été extrait de la cabine avant d'être évacué d'urgence vers Bobo-Dioulasso. C'est en milieu de journée, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026 aux alentours de 13 heures, qu'un drame de la circulation s'est déroulé à Nématoulaye, localité située dans la commune de Houndé, province du Tuy. Alors qu'il circulait sur la Route Nationale 1 (RN1), un camion-benne a brusquement quitté la chaussée. La course incontrôlée du poids lourd s'est achevée par un choc frontal et violent contre un arbre situé en bordure de route. La violence de l'impact n'a laissé aucune chance à l'apprenti-chauffeur. Touché mortellement lors de la collision, le jeune homme est décédé sur les lieux mêmes de l'accident. De son côté, le conducteur du poids lourd a été grièvement blessé lors de la percussion. Coincé à l'intérieur de l'habitacle endommagé, il a dû être extrait de la cabine avant d'être rapidement pris en charge et évacué vers Bobo-Dioulasso pour y recevoir des soins médicaux urgents. Selon le bureau de l'ONU pour la coordination des affaires humanitaires (Ocha), les attaques de colons ayant fait des victimes ou occasionné des dégâts matériels sont passées d'une moyenne de 1,5 par jour en 2021 à 6,7 au cours des huit premiers mois de 2026. items.title: Burkina : la CNLF saisit des marchandises illicites estimées à plus de 55 millions en 48 heures
items.description: La Coordination nationale de lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) a présenté, lundi à Ouagadougou, lors d’un point de presse, les résultats de trois opérations coup de poing menées les 30 septembre et 1er octobre 2026. Ces actions ont permis de saisir du cyanure, des cigarettes de contrebande, du gasoil subventionné détourné et de l’huile lubrifiante contrefaite, pour une valeur globale estimée à 55 233 000 FCFA. Selon le coordonnateur de la CNLF, Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, en l’espace de 48 heures, ses équipes ont asséné un coup dur aux réseaux de fraude et de contrebande opérant dans la capitale et ses environs. « La première prise a eu lieu le 1er octobre sur l’axe Ouaga-Koupéla », a-t-il souligné, indiquant que la fouille minutieuse d’un camion sous bâche censé transporter du clinker a permis de découvrir une cargaison camouflée comprenant 50 sacs de 50 kg de cyanure, estimés à une valeur de 7 500 000 FCFA, et 15 colis de cigarettes de contrebande, estimés à 3 450 000 FCFA, soit un total de 10 950 000 FCFA pour cette seule opération. Il a indiqué qu’auparavant, le 30 septembre 2026 à Loumbila, la CNLF avait mis au jour un réseau de détournement de carburant subventionné. Un camion-citerne a été pris en flagrant délit alors qu’il venait de dépoter 10 000 litres de gasoil dans les cuves d’une unité industrielle, avec un bon de commande destiné normalement aux stations-service pour la consommation ordinaire. Il a précisé que les investigations ont révélé qu’un cumul de 59 000 litres de gasoil subventionné par l’État, d’une valeur de 31 683 000 FCFA, avait été illégalement livré à cette entreprise par une société de droit burkinabè, en violation de la réglementation interdisant l’usage du carburant subventionné aux entreprises industrielles et minières. « Enfin, le 1er octobre 2026, au quartier Patte d’Oie de Ouagadougou, une alerte citoyenne a permis l’interception d’un véhicule transportant 267 cartons d’huile lubrifiante contrefaite et importée en contrebande, d’une valeur de 12 600 000 FCFA », a-t-il affirmé. Le coordonnateur national de lutte contre la fraude, Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, a salué le civisme des populations, dont les renseignements ont été déterminants pour la réussite de ces opérations. Il a réaffirmé la détermination de la CNLF à ne pas faiblir face aux fraudeurs qui menacent l’économie nationale, la santé publique et la sécurité. Los magistrados dejan su cumplimiento en manos de la Oficina del Censo Electoral y de los consulados que, ya antes de que se convocaran las elecciones generales para el 29 de noviembre, consideraban “materialmente imposible” culminar a tiempo para las elecciones autonómicas y municipales de mayo la revisión del Censo de Electores de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) que requiere la orden del Supremo. En sus autos de este lunes, la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo ha acordado, además, ofrecer a los afectados (163.020 personas, según la Abogacía) personarse en el procedimiento en el plazo de cinco días, lo que puede derivar en un aluvión de recursos de difícil gestión a mes y medio de las elecciones. items.title: “Cariño, ¿qué pasa dentro de un club de carretera?”
items.description: Una de las cosas que más me gustaba de tener pareja era ir de copiloto: suena Radio 5 Todo Noticias , se hace la noche y con ella el silencio, se encienden las largas, el uno va pendiente del asfalto, la otra del paisaje. Se comenta una noticia, se juntan las manos sobre la palanca de cambios, a lo mejor los dedos se deslizan jugones por la pernera. ¡Estate quieta! Risas. Una dice te quiero, el otro y yo. Los dos habitan una rara burbuja de intimidad, porque aunque un viaje es por definición un proyecto de futuro, en el coche solo existe el ahora. He recorrido carreteras del Norte, autopistas del Sur, vías rápidas del Este y calzadas del Oeste, enamorada del conductor y de la vida, porque la oxitocina produce cursilería y confianza ciegas. En esos viajes, no importa a dónde fuésemos, al mirar hacia un lado me topaba siempre con unos neones fluorescentes sobre algún edificio precario, con pinta de mueblería o de matadero, anunciando con el lenguaje tácito de los neones chillones que allí… ¿que allí qué? Acaba el boletín de las nueve, suena una de Coldplay o de U2. El conductor tararea. El morro del vehículo se come las rayas del asfalto a 120 kilómetros por hora. Oasis, Lady’s, Windsor, Paraíso, Zeus, Copacabana II, La Noche, Caribeña’s, Corazón, Huracán. Hay un club de alterne cada 1.750 metros. “Cariño, ¿qué crees que pasa ahí dentro?”. Él balbucea y yo qué sé. No tengo ni la más remota idea, repite ante la insistencia. Qué suerte tengo de haber encontrado a uno sin mácula en el país en el que los señores más recurren a la prostitución de Europa, ¿verdad? Por supuesto que jamás ha aparcado ahí fuera. No todos los hombres, aunque uno de cada tres. El reverso tenebroso de ese coche es la imagen que han escogido para el cartel de El Castillo , la serie basada en hechos reales magistralmente adaptada por varias señoras. Un hombre conduce por el interior de España, una mujer mira aterrorizada hacia su futuro. Sólo hay que verla y se acabaron las preguntas.

items.title: Cómo un buen café puede cambiar un negocio hostelero
items.description: ¿Por dónde empieza un buen café? ¿Por los ingredientes, por la forma de prepararlo, por la exigencia del cliente? “El primer paso es convencer a los hosteleros de que cambien su forma de prepararlo”, responde Raúl Villanueva, barista y formador de la marca Café Saula. Él, con dos décadas de experiencia en el sector hostelero, reconoce que deshacerse de las manías y automatismos puede ser complicado. Villanueva forma parte del equipo de seis formadores de Saula, la marca premium de café de Grupo Pascual, que recorren distintos locales del país para enseñar a los hosteleros a servir una bebida equilibrada, rica y estable; para que todas las tazas de café que sirvan tengan la misma calidad. “La resistencia al cambio impide sacar el máximo provecho del producto”, reflexiona. “La idea es culturizar a nuestros alumnos para que entiendan el café y sepan tratarlo mejor. Esto beneficia a todos: a nosotros como marca, a ellos como negocio y a su cliente final”, sostiene. Seguir leyendo

items.title: AJK leaders call for peaceful resolution of Poonch crisis
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Political leaders in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) have called for a pe­­aceful and dignified resolution of the crisis in Poo­nch division, while ex­­pres­sing concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in the region. The call was made at a meeting hosted by Muslim Conference president Sar­dar Attique Ahmed Khan at his Rawalpindi residence on Monday. The meeting was atte­n­ded by PPP leader Sardar Yaqoob Khan, PML-N AJK president Shah Ghulam Qadir, PML-N leader Raja Farooq Haider, leader of the opposition in AJK Assembly Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin, and Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party AJK President Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and others. According to a statement, the participants called for the restoration of internet services, uninterrupted supplies of food and medicines, and the resumption of communication links and free movement in Poonch division. They also demanded that eligible voters in the region be allowed to participate in the electoral process without delay. The meeting expressed deep concern over the law and order situation in AJK, particularly in Poonch division, and called for a political settlement of the crisis through peaceful and dignified means. items.title: Legal fraternity rails against emergency proclamation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
items.description: Lawyers scuffle with police during a protest in Lahore condemning the imposition of emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.—AFP • PBC members question constitutional basis for invoking Articles 232 and 234 • IHCBA describes governor’s rule as an attack on public mandate and provincial autonomy • LHCBA and LBA to challenge the move in Supreme Court • KBA seeks withdrawal of emergency, restoration of govt • KPBC to observe ‘black day’ and boycott court proceedings today ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: The legal community and bar bodies have condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), with the Lahore High Court Bar Association (LHCBA) and the Lahore Bar Association (LBA) deciding on Monday to challenge the move before the Supreme Court through a constitutional petition. Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC), in a statement, condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP and called upon the president to immediately withdraw what they described as the “unconstitutional proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule”. They also urged the president to immediately restore the democraticall-elected KP government and respect provincial autonomy. They maintained that the president’s invocation of Articles 232 and 234 on the advice of the prime minister and the cabinet was illegal and unconstitutional. Under Article 232, the statement pointed out, the proclamation of an emergency on grounds of internal disturbance beyond the control of a provincial government requires a resolution of the provincial assembly. No such resolution had been passed, the signatories noted. It added that Article 234 permits governor’s rule only when the government of a province cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. However, the provincial government and assembly were both performing their functions in accordance with the Constitution, the signatories maintained. ‘Attack on public mandate’ Separately, the Islamabad High Court Bar Association (IHCBA) has also strongly condemned the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, describing it as an attack on the public mandate, democratic values and provincial autonomy. In a statement issued by its secretary, the association said it would vigorously oppose any attempt to suppress the will of the people through the exercise of administrative powers. The statement said constitutional supremacy, parliamentary democracy and provincial autonomy were the foundations of Pakistan’s constitutional system, adding that extraordinary constitutional measures should not be used to undermine an elected government. members of the Karachi Bar Association hold placards and chant slogans during a general body meeting.—AFP Constitutional petition On the other hand, the LHCBA and the LBA have decided to file a constitutional petition in the Supreme Court challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. The decision was taken at a joint general house meeting, which expressed concern over the country’s constitutional and political situation and the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. A resolution unanimously adopted by the house stated that the move would be challenged in light of constitutional and legal principles to enable judicial scrutiny of its legality and safeguard the requirements of the Constitution, the rule of law, democracy and provincial autonomy. ‘Lift emergency’ The Karachi Bar Association (KBA) demanded that the federal government lift the emergency imposed in KP and restore the provincial government. The demand was made at a general body meeting, where KBA President Aamir Nawaz Warraich said: “If we do not take a stand today, a stage will come when we will be unable to do anything.” He added that the imposition of emergency was the first step towards martial law. Black day Meanwhile, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council (KPBC) expressed concern over the imposition of emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution and announced that it would observe a ‘black day’ on Tuesday (today) and boycott court proceedings. In a statement issued here, the KPBC said the imposition of emergency was an extraordinary constitutional measure. The council announced that it would observe a ‘black day’ on Tuesday and refrain from appearing in courts. Also, the All Pakistan Lawyers Action Committee (APLAC) condemned the imposition of governor’s rule in KP and arrests of the elected chief minister and parliamentarians. In a statement, APLAC Chairman Ali Ahmed Kurd strongly condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, as well as the arrests of the province’s ‘non functional’ CM Sohail Afridi, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and other members of parliament. Sumair Abdullah in Karachi, Umer Farooq in Peshawar and Saleem Shahid in Quetta also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: UNESCO : le monde aura besoin de 50 millions d’enseignants supplémentaires d’ici 2030
items.description: L'Organisation des Nations unies pour l'éducation, la science et la culture (UNESCO), a estimé que le monde dispose actuellement de 107 millions d’enseignants, mais il en faudrait 50 millions de plus d’ici 2030 pour garantir l’accès universel à l’éducation préprimaire, primaire et secondaire. Dans sa nouvelle fiche d’information concernant la profession, dévoilée à l’occasion de la célébration cette semaine de la Journée mondiale des enseignants 2026, l'Organisation affirme que « cela signifie que 50 % d’enseignants supplémentaires sont nécessaires ». Soixante ans après l’adoption de la Recommandation OIT/UNESCO de 1966 concernant la condition du personnel enseignant, la nouvelle fiche d’information publiée par l’Institut de statistique de l’UNESCO et l’Équipe spéciale internationale sur les enseignants pour Éducation 2030 analyse le statut des enseignants, y compris leur valorisation, le soutien et la rémunération qu’ils reçoivent. Elle évoque des enjeux « majeurs » alors que les estimations suggèrent qu’à l’échelle mondiale, 58 % des enseignants nécessaires d’ici 2030 devraient remplacer ceux qui quitteront le métier. La fiche d’information identifie les plus grandes pertes : les taux de déperdition sont de 7,2 % pour l’enseignement préprimaire, 4,7 % pour le primaire et 5,4 % pour le secondaire. Le document propose des recommandations pratiques pour les gouvernements et les partenaires visant notamment à impliquer les enseignants dans la préparation des politiques et à définir des standards et des parcours professionnels, tout en les encourageant à offrir une rémunération compétitive et des incitations ciblées pour les établissements qui manquent de personnel, rendre les écoles plus sûres et plus solidaires du corps enseignant, et réduire la charge de travail non nécessaire. La fiche d’information a été publiée pour marquer la Journée mondiale des enseignants 2026, qui a réuni des ministres, des enseignants et des experts de l’éducation au siège de l’UNESCO à Paris, afin d’échanger sur les solutions qui pourraient consolider la profession. Co-organisée par l’UNESCO, l’Organisation internationale du travail (OIT), l’UNICEF et l’Internationale de l’éducation, la célébration a eu pour thème « Aux côtés du personnel enseignant : 60 ans à protéger la profession, promouvoir la condition enseignante et façonner nos futurs ». « Chaque apprenant mérite un enseignant qui est bien préparé, qui bénéficie d’un soutien adéquat et qui peut s’épanouir dans sa profession », soulignaient l’UNESCO, l’OIT, l’UNICEF et l’Internationale de l’éducation, dans leur message commun à cette occasion. Les organisations partenaires se disent convaincues que « la concrétisation de ce droit dépend de la valeur que les sociétés accordent aux enseignants et à la profession enseignante ». En réalité, relève l'UNESCO, « la valeur que nous accordons aux enseignants reflète celle que nous accordons aux générations futures » . The post UNESCO : le monde aura besoin de 50 millions d’enseignants supplémentaires d’ici 2030 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: CHU Yalgado Ouédraogo : Avis de recherche du patient Fousseni Sawadogo, évadé du service de psychiatrie
items.description: Un avis de recherche a été émis à la suite de la disparition d'un patient au service de psychiatrie du Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) Yalgado Ouédraogo. Le nommé Fousseni Sawadogo, récemment rentré de Côte d'Ivoire, s'est évadé de l'établissement au cours de la nuit du 11 octobre. Un appel à la vigilance est lancé pour aider sa famille et les services de santé à le localiser au plus vite. L'alerte a été donnée au Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) Yalgado Ouédraogo. Au cours de la nuit du 11 octobre, le jeune Fousseni Sawadogo s'est évadé du service de psychiatrie où il était admis en hospitalisation. Revenu depuis peu de la Côte d'Ivoire, le jeune homme se trouvait sous prise en charge médicale au moment de sa fuite. Afin de permettre sa localisation rapide, un avis de recherche a été diffusé auprès du public. Toute personne disposant d'informations permettant de retrouver Fousseni Sawadogo est priée de prendre d'urgence attache avec son oncle au téléphone au 46 79 78 34 . La collaboration de la population est vivement sollicitée pour aider la famille dans ses recherches. L’article CHU Yalgado Ouédraogo : Avis de recherche du patient Fousseni Sawadogo, évadé du service de psychiatrie est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Riyadh vows ‘serious’ response amid Houthi escalation
items.description: • Saudi minister says ‘energy security can’t be taken for granted’ • Yemeni rebels warn of ‘swift, painful response’ if US joins war • Iran ‘deeply concerned’, offers to help broker talks • Riyadh airport to remain shut RIYADH: Saudi Arabia vowed a “serious” response after Houthi strikes turned Riyadh’s international airport into a target, killing 18 people in under a week and leaving the world’s biggest oil exporter facing its worst security crisis in more than a decade. “Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious. For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people and our resilience.” The strikes have shaken the world’s biggest oil exporter, which is pursuing an expensive economic reform programme intended to att­ract foreign investment. Oil prices rose above $105 a barrel on Monday. Yemen’s civil war, in which a Saudi-led military coalition backs the government against the Houthis, has reignited months into the wider US-Iran conflict, which has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis. On Saturday, Houthi strikes killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 at King Khalid International Airport, the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Four people died in earlier attacks on Wed­nes­day and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday, when Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said a fresh strike also wounded 11 people. Riyadh’s airport was not the only one to suffer an attack as authorities said Dammam airport in the east was also struck on Sunday evening. One person had been killed and 11 wounded in a strike on Dammam airport. The Saudi-led coalition said on Monday it had “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for Khamis Mushait, a southern city that is home to a major military base. It also reported responding to drone and missile threats around Riyadh, where residents reported explosions and authorities warned of continuing security risks. The coalition has called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”. Volker Turk, the UN human rights chief, said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia but urged both sides to back down. US warned against joining strikes A Houthi official warned on Monday that the US would face a “swift and painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen. Donald Trump has said he is considering joining Saudi strikes against the group. “If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthi political bureau, told AFP. He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”. The campaign, he said, was intended to show the crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”. Trump condemned Saturday’s attack as “not acceptable” and said he would speak to the crown prince about the possibility of joining strikes against the Houthis. Fighting in Taiz Elsewhere in Yemen, Houthi fighters have tightened their siege of Taiz, where more than 60 people were killed in 24 hours, military sources from both sides told AFP. A military source loyal to the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government said the Houthis had blocked all exits and launched several attacks overnight. The dead included 22 pro-government fighters and at least 40 Houthis, the sources said. The Houthis continued fighting despite Saudi airstrikes and were sending reinforcements. Yemen’s health ministry warned on Sunday of a “humanitarian catastrophe” in the city, where medicine, medical equipment and fuel were “on the verge of running out”. Regional reaction Iran said it was “deeply concerned” about the escalating attacks between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia and offered to help broker talks. “We are deeply concerned about the developments taking place in the Arabian Peninsula,” the foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baqaei, told a weekly news conference. Tehran was ready, he said, “to use our good offices to help facilitate dialogue between the parties”. Anwar Gargash, a diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, called for stronger Gulf security cooperation. “It is necessary to revive joint action by the Gulf countries, particularly in security and defence, and to strengthen the collective security system,” he wrote on X, adding that shortcomings in regional security had encouraged further attacks. The UAE, which has long been at odds with Saudi Arabia over Yemen, expressed its “full solidarity” with the kingdom. China also condemned the attacks on Saudi airports and energy infrastructure. “China condemns the attacks that caused heavy casualties and expresses serious concern over the intensification of the conflict,” said the foreign ministry spoke­swoman, Mao Ning, who urged all parties to avoid escalation and resolve disputes through dialogue. Flights disrupted Authorities have extended the closure of King Khalid international airport until Saturday, and airlines have cancelled flights after the repeated attacks. A notice to airmen showed the airport would stay closed until 2100 GMT on Oct 17. Flightradar24 showed aircraft avoiding Riyadh on Monday, although flights continued through Saudi airspace towards Jeddah. The aviation analytics firm Cirium said cancellations across Saudi airports had reached 46.4pc. Etihad Airways cancelled flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah, while Gulf Air suspended services to Riyadh. Lufthansa and Air France-KLM also extended suspensions. Delta Air Lines postponed its planned Atlanta-Riyadh service, due to start on Oct 23, until March 2027. US aviation regulators urged airlines to exercise caution, and the American embassy warned citizens of security risks. “This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented,” said Mark Zee, the founder of the aviation safety organisation Opsgroup. Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says
items.description: By David Lawder BANGKOK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday. Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1%, a slight uptick from the 3.0% it predicted in July.

items.title: Super El Nino set to make 2026 record hottest year
items.description: BRUSSELS: An intensifying El Nino pattern set an all-time temperature high in a key Pacific zone in September and could help make this year the hottest globally on record, the director of the EU’s climate monitor said on Monday. Global forecasters have been warning for months that this El Nino would likely become the strongest ever observed and the latest record has tumbled even before the episode’s expected peak later this year. The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming. The Copernicus Clim­ate Change Service said sea surface temperatures in a tell-tale El Nino monitoring region of the Pacific, known as Nino3.4, had reached an “all-time high” of 29.70 degrees Celsius last month. This exceeded the peak temperatures of previously strong El Nino events of 1982/1983, 1997/1998 and 2015/2016, the EU monitor said. This year’s El Nino, which emerged in June, is “very exceptional” but it is too early to say whether it is the strongest ever observed, Copernicus director Carlo Buontempo told AFP. As climate change raises ocean temperatures, it can make recent El Nino events appear stronger than past ones, complicating historical comparisons. Copernicus said it had adopted a new index, which accounts for the warming of tropical oceans, that suggested the current event is not yet stronger than past ones. “It’s a very large event even in that metric,” Buontempo said. “This very large event today is happening in a much warmer climate.” Not all forecasters use the same scale to interpret El Nino. On Friday, Japan’s weather agency said that El Nino conditions had reached their “strongest intensity on record”. Record ocean temperatures As El Nino gathers strength, global average sea surface temperatures hit a record 21.05 degrees Celsius for September, topping the previous high of 20.92 for the same month in 2023, according to Copernicus. Experts have warned that this El Nino, combined with human-induced climate change, could make 2027 the hottest year on record as heat stored in the Pacific is released into the atmosphere. The weather phenomenon, which typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months, can drive world temperatures higher the year after its peak. But Buontempo said even 2026 could wind up a record breaker as this El Nino builds toward its peak. “If we follow the pattern we have seen in the past, we may have a record-breaking 2026, followed by a record-breaking 2027,” he told AFP. After a record-breaking August, the world experienced its second hottest September ever observed, with surface air temperatures averaging 16.27 degrees Celsius, the EU service said. Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: Paris Motor Show opens with record number of Chinese brands
items.description: The 91st Paris Motor Show opened in the French capital on Monday, with a record number of Chinese automakers taking part to showcase their latest models and technologies. The week-long event brings together over 100 exhibitors and more than 60 automakers. A total of 25 Chinese brands, represented by 16 automakers including BYD, XPeng, Changan, Dongfeng and Leapmotor, are taking part in the show, roughly double the number at the 2024 edition. Serge Gachot, director of the Paris Motor Show, said that compared with two years ago, Chinese automakers are placing greater emphasis on raising brand awareness while stepping up efforts to seek local partners, demonstrating a stronger commitment to the French and broader European markets. Besides Chinese automakers, European brands including Audi, Citroen, Peugeot, Renault and Volkswagen are also presenting new models and electrification technologies, making electric vehicles, intelligent driving and innovative mobility solutions among the key highlights of this year's show. For the first time, the Paris Motor Show has introduced autonomous-driving demonstrations for the public. Visitors can learn how the technologies work and ride in vehicles equipped with intelligent driving systems to experience their functions in real-world road conditions. The event has also expanded its test-drive program, offering around 90 models from 20 automotive brands, including battery electric vehicles and hybrid vehicles. More than 5,000 test drives are planned during the show, allowing visitors to experience the performance and technological features of the latest models. Held every two years, the Paris Motor Show spans five halls, with 70,000 square meters of indoor exhibition space and an additional 15,000 square meters of outdoor space this year.

items.description: Noam Cohen was driving to a bar on a Saturday two years ago with his wife and friends in his hometown of Arad, in southern Israel, when a group of ultra-Orthodox Jewish boys began shouting at passing cars. items.title: Dar-led body to oversee KP affairs
items.description: ISLAMABAD: After im­p­­o­sing an emergency in the province, Prime Mini­ster Shehbaz Sharif for­med an 11-member committee headed by his deputy Ishaq Dar to oversee the affairs of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. A source close to the premier told Dawn that the committee was formed informally and that no official notification had been issued about its formation, but the body would monitor governance and security issues in KP daily and report to the PM. The body will maintain close liaison with the new setup in KP and provide assistance in the discharge of its (KP Advisory Council) duties and security-related matters. According to the source, Law Minister Azam Nazir Tarar, Minister for Plan­ning and Development Ahsan Iqbal, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Minister for Kashmir Aff­airs Amir Muqam, Mini­ster for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chau­dhry, Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) Convener Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, PM’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah, and one member each from the PPP, the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), and the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) are part of the committee led by Mr Dar. Earlier, the PM formed an 11-member KP Advi­sory Board or a ‘cabinet’ of Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to run the affairs of the province. Parliament meets today Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari summoned sessions of the Senate and the National Assembly today (Tuesday) at 6pm. The sessions were called apparently to get the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule in KP endorsed to meet a constitutional requirement. Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel said the period of emergency and governor’s rule could be more than six months. In a statement, he said the length of the emergency will depend on the security situation in KP. Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: ‘Pakistan’s poverty rate higher than India, B’desh’
items.description: WASHINGTON: More than one-third of Pakistan’s population faces overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards, according to the United Nations Development Prog­ramme’s (UNDP) Multidimensional Pov­er­ty Index (MPI) released on Monday. Figures released by the UNDP in New York show that 38.3 per cent of Pakistan’s population was multidimensionally poor, compared with 16.4 per cent in India and 14.9pc in Bangladesh. The estimates are based on household surveys conducted in different years and do not provide a strictly contemporaneous comparison. In Pakistan, the intensity of deprivation among those classified as multidimensionally poor stood at 51.7pc. Another 12.9pc of the population was considered vulnerable to multidimensional poverty, indicating that a substantial share of people remained at risk of falling into acute deprivation. Unlike conventional income-based measures, the MPI assesses overlapping disadvantages in areas such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing and household assets. UNDP estimates 38.3pc Pakistanis face multidimensional poverty The report also documents a worrying global reversal. The number of people living in multidimensional poverty has risen for the first time in 15 years, reaching 1.2 billion, as families struggle to meet their basic needs. The latest total is 51.5 million higher than the previous update. Children account for more than half of those affected, with 617m living in multidimensional poverty, while 83pc of the total live in rural areas. The global findings underline the scale of the challenge facing governments, particularly in providing essential services to disadvantaged communities. Poverty is not simply a shortage of income; it can also mean inadequate nutrition, missed schooling and a lack of clean water or electricity. South Asia accounts for a substantial share of global deprivation. The report says the region accounts for at least one-third of global deprivations in nutrition, housing, and years of schooling. It is also home to 150m poor people living in households where a school-aged child is not attending school, highlighting persistent barriers to education despite broader development gains. The UNDP’s regional figures put South Asia’s multidimensional poverty rate at approximately 19.3pc, with another 18.4pc of the population vulnerable to such poverty. Health accounts for about 29.9pc of the contribution to regional multidimensional poverty, education for 33.7pc and living standards for 36.3pc. The figures show how disadvantages in different areas reinforce one another. Poor health, inadequate education and substandard living conditions can trap families in poverty and make it difficult for them to improve their circumstances. “The rise in poverty should be a wake-up call for the world,” said UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo. “Behind these figures are 1.2 billion people facing hardships that reinforce one another: hunger, missed schooling and a lack of clean water or electricity. This is unacceptable.” Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: El FMI vuelve a situar a España como la gran economía que más crece en 2026
items.description: La economía de los países desarrollados sigue dando sorpresas positivas pese a tener en contra a sus principales enemigos: la inflación y una deuda pública desbocada. El Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) ha revisado al alza sus previsiones, con España liderando la corrección al alza. El FMI dice ahora que crecerá un 2,5%, cuatro décimas más de lo que pronosticaba hace meses, pero todavía una décima por debajo de la cifra que prevé el consenso de economistas (y el propio Gobierno de España). Las revisiones al alza sobre el crecimiento de España se han vuelto algo frecuente para el organismo, que tiende a infraestimar el desempeño de la economía española. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ex-GB chief minister among several PTI leaders arrested
items.description: • Khalid Khurshid, Babar Saleem Swati detained from KP Assembly speaker’s house in Peshawar • Police claim Khurshid is wanted in connection with multiple criminal cases GILGIT: Former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and PTI’s regional president Khalid Khurshid Khan was arrested along with KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and several others at the speaker’s house in Peshawar on Sunday night, according to the party’s official social media page. A police source also confirmed the arrest of PTI’s GB chapter president, saying the former chief minister was wanted in multiple criminal cases. “Khalid Khurshid and others have been arrested from the speaker’s residence in Peshawar,” the police source said. Sources said Mr Khurshid had been staying at the KP chief minister’s residence since 2023 to avoid arrest by GB police. He reportedly moved to the assembly speaker’s residence on Sunday after the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in KP. Sources could not confirm whether Mr Khurshid would be transferred to GB for court proceedings or taken to another city. Arrest orders In December 2024, an anti-terrorism court in Gilgit-Baltistan sentenced Mr Khurshid to 34 years in prison and imposed a fine of Rs600,000 for threatening security institutions during a public gathering. Anti-Terrorism Court Judge Rehmat Shah also directed the GB inspector general of police to arrest Mr Khurshid and ordered the director general of the National Database and Registration Authority to block his national identity card. Mr Khurshid had failed to appear before the court despite repeated notices issued during the proceedings. The former chief minister was also named in several police cases related to PTI protests and alleged confrontations with law enforcement authorities in Lahore and Islamabad. In March 2023, he was accused of using GB police personnel and government resources to provide security for former prime minister Imran Khan during efforts by authorities to arrest the PTI founder in Lahore. The action followed the federal government’s collection of evidence concerning the alleged use of GB police personnel and resou­rces for Imran Khan’s security. Mr Khurshid also faced allegations of using official resources to support PTI demonstrations. Disqualification Mr Khurshid was elected to the Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly from the Astore district on a PTI ticket in the 2020 general elections and subsequently became chief minister. In July 2023, the GB Chief Court disqualified him from holding public office over allegations that he had obtained a licence from the GB Bar Council using a fraudulent educational degree. The ruling ended his tenure as chief minister and triggered a political realignment in the region. Following his disqualification, several PTI lawmakers broke ranks with the party, paving the way for the formation of a coalition government. Haji Gulbar Khan, a dissident PTI lawmaker, subsequently became the new chief minister of the region. Despite the court orders and multiple criminal cases, Mr Khurshid had remained outside the custody of GB police until his reported arrest on Sunday. Published in Dawn, October 13th, 2026

items.title: Shanghai wins first WIPO City of Innovation award
items.description: Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced on Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. Launched in 2026, the WIPO City of Innovation award is open to cities across all 194 WIPO member states and is bestowed on visionary cities for their bold pledges to foster innovation and creativity over the coming year. The three winners were chosen from 15 finalist cities. According to WIPO, Shanghai's vision is to strengthen its position as an international hub for science, technology and intellectual property (IP), while fostering a broader culture of innovation and creativity. Its pledges include expanding IP education and services, opening innovation infrastructure and data, supporting cultural and creative industries, and strengthening connections between research, industry, entrepreneurs and investors. Zhou Yaming, deputy secretary-general of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, said the award represents WIPO's strong recognition of Shanghai's innovative developments and its efforts in building a thriving IP ecosystem. "It also reflects the international community's endorsement of China's commitment to open innovation, mutual benefits and shared success," he said. Winners were selected by an independent international jury of high-profile experts in the cultural and creative, urban planning, community development and innovation-driven growth sectors. Andrea Dempster Chung, member of the International Jury Panel and co-founder and executive director for Kingston Creative, said Shanghai's application was extremely impressive, not just because of the strong research and development base that the city already had, but for the sheer scale of its ambitions and the strength of pledges. "This would be pivotal in shifting the city's future and this is one of the reasons why Shanghai was selected," she said.

items.title: Carnet noir à l’École nationale de police : L’élève sous-officier Jules TIENDREBEOGO emporté par un accident de la route
items.description: L’École nationale de police est plongée dans le deuil à la suite du décès tragique de l’élève sous-officier de première année Jules TIENDREBEOGO, survenu dans la nuit du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026 lors d’un accident de la circulation. Inhumé le dimanche 11 octobre au cimetière de Tanlarghin, le jeune élève de la 56ᵉ promotion laisse derrière lui des camarades et une hiérarchie affligés par cette disparition brutale. L'École nationale de police a été frappée par la perte tragique de l'un de ses apprenants. Dans la nuit du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026, l'élève sous-officier de police de première année Jules TIENDREBEOGO a perdu la vie à la suite d'un accident de la circulation routière. La triste nouvelle a été officiellement portée à la connaissance de la communauté par le Directeur général de l'établissement. L'inhumation du défunt s'est déroulée dans l'après-midi du dimanche 11 octobre 2026 au cimetière de Tanlarghin, où proches, parents et frères d'armes se sont rassemblés pour lui rendre un ultime hommage. Face à cette douloureuse épreuve, le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Directeur général de l’École nationale de police ainsi que l’ensemble du personnel administratif et d’encadrement ont témoigné de leur profonde affliction. Les autorités ont adressé leurs condoléances les plus sincères à la famille éplorée, aux proches du disparu ainsi qu’à l'ensemble de ses camarades de la 56ᵉ promotion. Toute l'institution s'est unie dans le recueillement pour saluer la mémoire de l'élève policier et prier pour le repos de son âme.
